scenarios.context_ko: 바쁜 친구와 이번 주 저녁 약속 날짜·장소 조율

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, are you free any night this week? I feel like we haven't hung out in ages.
dialogue.ko: 야, 이번 주 저녁에 시간 돼? 우리 너무 오래 못 봤잖아.
alt_en: You free this week? It's been forever.
Any chance you have a night free? We're overdue.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: This week is kind of packed. Wednesday maybe?
dialogue.ko: 이번 주는 좀 빡빡해. 수요일은 어떨까?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Wednesday works. Evening, like around seven?
dialogue.ko: 수요일 괜찮아. 저녁, 7시쯤?
alt_en: Wednesday's good. Seven-ish?
Works for me — evening around seven?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Seven's good. Where are you thinking?
dialogue.ko: 7시 좋아. 어디 생각해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That Korean BBQ place near the station. Or, uh, somewhere else if you want.
dialogue.ko: 역 근처 한국식 바베큐 집. 아니면, 음, 다른 데 가고 싶으면.
alt_en: The KBBQ spot near the station — unless you want something different.
I was thinking Korean BBQ by the station. Open to other ideas though.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: KBBQ sounds perfect actually. Haven't been in a while.
dialogue.ko: 한국 바베큐 딱 좋겠다. 오랜만이기도 하고.
dialogue.recast_note: 'Korean BBQ place' → 'KBBQ' 약칭으로 더 자연스러운 구어 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Great. Should I make a reservation, or are they usually okay without one?
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 예약할까, 아니면 보통 예약 없어도 돼?
alt_en: I'll book it if needed — do they take reservations?
Want me to reserve? Or can we just walk in?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Better to book — it gets busy after seven. I'll text you the address.
dialogue.ko: 예약하는 게 나아 — 7시 이후로 바빠져. 주소 문자로 보낼게.

key_expressions.note: 친구 사이에서 오랜 공백 표현. ages = 오랫동안
바쁜 일정 표현. 'very busy'보다 자연스럽다
권고 표현. 'You should book'보다 부드럽다

common_mistakes_ko: 'We didn't meet for a long time' → 'We haven't hung out in ages' (hang out = 어울리다)
'My schedule is full' → 'It's kind of packed' (일정 꽉 찼다는 구어체)
'Make a reservation' 대신 'book' 단독 사용이 구어체에서 더 자연스럽다

scenarios.context_ko: 잡아둔 약속 시간을 변경해야 해서 친구에게 양해 구하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, sorry to do this, but can we push our plans back an hour?
dialogue.ko: 야, 미안한데, 우리 약속 한 시간 뒤로 미뤄도 될까?
alt_en: So sorry, but could we move our meetup back an hour?
Hate to ask, but is an hour later okay?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh yeah, totally fine. What came up?
dialogue.ko: 아 그래, 완전 괜찮아. 무슨 일이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Work thing ran longer than expected. I'm still at the office, uh, wrapping things up.
dialogue.ko: 회사 일이 예상보다 길어졌어. 아직 사무실에 있어, 음, 마무리 중.
alt_en: Meeting ran over. Still finishing up at work.
Got held up at the office — should be done soon.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No worries, happens to everyone. So instead of seven, we're saying eight?
dialogue.ko: 걱정 마, 누구나 있어. 그럼 7시 말고 8시로?
dialogue.recast_note: 'push back an hour' → 'instead of seven, eight'로 구체적 시간으로 확인하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, eight works. I should be out by seven-thirty, so I'll have time.
dialogue.ko: 응, 8시. 7시 반엔 나올 수 있을 것 같으니까 여유 있어.
alt_en: Eight's perfect — I'll be out by seven-thirty.
Eight, yes. I'll have buffer time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Cool. Same place?
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 장소는 같은 데?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, same spot. Thanks for being flexible.
dialogue.ko: 응, 같은 데. 맞춰줘서 고마워.
alt_en: Same place. Really appreciate you being cool about it.
Same spot — thanks for working with me on this.

key_expressions.note: 일정·약속을 늦추는 표현. 'postpone'보다 구어적
일·회의가 예상 시간을 초과했을 때
상대방의 양보에 감사할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'Delay our meeting' → 'push back our plans' / 'move it back an hour' (약속 미루기 구어 표현)
'push back'을 '거절하다' 의미로 혼동 주의 — 시간 맥락에선 '뒤로 미루다'
'Thanks for understanding' → 'Thanks for being flexible' (더 구체적인 감사 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 약속 당일 몸이 안 좋아서 취소 연락하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, I'm really sorry — I can't make it tonight. I'm not feeling well.
dialogue.ko: 야, 진짜 미안한데 — 오늘 저녁 못 갈 것 같아. 몸이 안 좋아.
alt_en: So sorry to bail, but I'm not doing well today.
I hate to do this, but I'm sick — can't make it tonight.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh no, what's wrong? Are you okay?
dialogue.ko: 아이고, 어디가 안 좋아? 괜찮아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Nothing serious, I think. Just a headache and, uh, kind of tired all day.
dialogue.ko: 심각한 건 아닌 것 같아. 그냥 두통이랑, 음, 하루 종일 피곤했어.
alt_en: Probably just a cold — headache and fatigue.
Just drained. Headache that won't quit.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sounds like you've been running on empty. Rest is the right call.
dialogue.ko: 완전 방전된 것 같네. 쉬는 게 맞아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'tired all day' → 'running on empty'로 더 표현력 있게 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. I feel bad canceling last minute like this.
dialogue.ko: 그러게. 이렇게 직전에 취소해서 미안해.
alt_en: I really do feel bad about this.
Sorry for the short notice — I hate doing this.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Don't worry about it. Health first. Can we reschedule for next week?
dialogue.ko: 걱정 마. 건강이 먼저야. 다음 주로 다시 잡을까?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Definitely. Thursday or Friday works for me next week.
dialogue.ko: 물론이지. 다음 주 목요일이나 금요일은 돼.
alt_en: Yes — next Thursday or Friday, either works.
Absolutely. I'm free most of next week.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Let's say Friday. Feel better, okay?
dialogue.ko: 금요일로 하자. 빨리 나아.

key_expressions.note: 구어체. 'cancel on someone'보다 캐주얼
연료가 없는 차처럼 에너지가 다 떨어진 상태
'last minute notice'와 유사. 미리 알리지 못한 것에 대한 사과 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Cancel the promise' → 'cancel our plans' / 'bail on you' (약속 취소 구어 표현)
'I am sick' 만으로 끝내기 — 구체적 증상(headache, fatigue 등)을 덧붙이면 더 자연스럽다
'Next week can we meet?' → 'Can we reschedule for next week?' (다시 잡기 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 미용실에 전화해서 원하는 날짜와 서비스 예약하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Thank you for calling Bloom Salon. How can I help you?
dialogue.ko: 블룸 살롱입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi, I'd like to make an appointment for a haircut.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 헤어컷 예약하고 싶어서요.
alt_en: Hello — I'm looking to book a haircut.
Hi, can I schedule a haircut?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Of course. Do you have a preferred day?
dialogue.ko: 물론이죠. 원하시는 날짜 있으세요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: This Saturday if possible. Sometime in the afternoon.
dialogue.ko: 가능하면 이번 토요일로요. 오후 중으로요.
alt_en: Saturday, if you have something open in the afternoon.
This Saturday afternoon, if there's availability.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: We have two-thirty or four o'clock on Saturday. Which works better?
dialogue.ko: 토요일에 2시 30분이랑 4시가 있어요. 어느 쪽이 더 좋으세요?
dialogue.recast_note: 'sometime in the afternoon' → 구체적 시간 두 개로 좁혀서 제시하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Two-thirty would be great.
dialogue.ko: 2시 30분으로 해주세요.
alt_en: Two-thirty works perfectly.
I'll take the two-thirty slot.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Perfect. Can I get your name and a number to confirm?
dialogue.ko: 좋습니다. 성함과 연락처를 알려주시겠어요?

key_expressions.note: 공식 예약. 'book'과 같이 쓸 수 있다
요청 시 부드럽게 조건 달기
예약 시간을 선택할 때 사용하는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to reservation' → 'I'd like to make an appointment' (reservation은 식당·호텔, appointment는 미용실·병원)
'When is available?' → 'Do you have availability on Saturday?' / '...this Saturday afternoon?'
'I choose 2:30' → 'Two-thirty works' / 'I'll take two-thirty' (선택 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 잡아둔 치과 예약 날짜를 바꾸도록 요청하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Greenville Dental, how can I help you?
dialogue.ko: 그린빌 치과입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi, I need to change my appointment. My name is Sumin Chae.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 예약을 변경해야 할 것 같아서요. 채수민입니다.
alt_en: Hello — I'm calling to reschedule. I'm Sumin Chae.
Hi, I'd like to move my appointment. Sumin Chae.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Let me pull that up. You're scheduled for Thursday at ten, correct?
dialogue.ko: 확인해볼게요. 목요일 10시로 되어 있으시죠?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's right. Something came up Thursday, so I need to reschedule.
dialogue.ko: 맞아요. 목요일에 일이 생겨서 변경이 필요해요.
alt_en: Yes, that's me. I have a conflict Thursday.
Correct — I can't make it Thursday anymore.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No problem. Any preference for day or time?
dialogue.ko: 알겠습니다. 요일이나 시간 선호하시는 게 있으세요?
dialogue.recast_note: 'I need to reschedule' → 'No problem' + 새 일정 탐색으로 자연스럽게 이어받으며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Next week if possible. Morning is better for me.
dialogue.ko: 가능하면 다음 주로요. 오전이 더 나아요.
alt_en: Next week, mornings work best.
Anytime next week, preferably morning.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: We have Monday at nine or Tuesday at nine-thirty. Which works?
dialogue.ko: 월요일 9시, 화요일 9시 30분이 있어요. 어느 쪽이 괜찮으세요?

key_expressions.note: 예상치 못한 사정이 생겼을 때. 구체적 이유를 말하지 않아도 된다
시스템에서 정보를 꺼낼 때
취소가 아닌 변경 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to change my reservation' → 'I need to reschedule my appointment' (병원은 reservation 대신 appointment)
'Something happened' → 'Something came up' (갑작스러운 사정 표현)
'Morning time' → 'mornings' / 'morning is better' (시간대 선호 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 팀 미팅 일정을 조율하면서 참석 가능 시간 확인하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, I'm trying to find a time for the team to sync next week. When are you free?
dialogue.ko: 안녕, 다음 주 팀 미팅 시간 잡으려고. 언제 시간 돼?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm pretty open Tuesday and Thursday. What time are you thinking?
dialogue.ko: 화요일이랑 목요일은 꽤 여유 있어. 몇 시 생각하고 있어?
alt_en: Tuesday or Thursday work for me. What time are you aiming for?
I'm free most of Tuesday and Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I was thinking afternoon. Around two or three?
dialogue.ko: 오후로 생각하고 있어. 2시나 3시쯤?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thursday at two works for me. Though, uh, I'd need to leave by three-thirty.
dialogue.ko: 목요일 2시 괜찮아. 다만, 음, 3시 반엔 나가야 해.
alt_en: Thursday two is fine — I have a hard stop at three-thirty.
Thursday at two works. I'll need to wrap by three-thirty.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hard stop at three-thirty — noted. One hour should be enough. I'll send the invite.
dialogue.ko: 3시 반 마감 — 알겠어. 한 시간이면 충분할 거야. 초대장 보낼게.
dialogue.recast_note: 'leave by three-thirty' → 'hard stop at three-thirty'로 업무 용어로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Great. Should I prepare anything beforehand?
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 미리 준비할 게 있어?
alt_en: Perfect. Anything I should bring or prep?
Sounds good. Any prep work on my end?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Just bring your Q3 numbers. That's it.
dialogue.ko: 3분기 수치만 갖고 와. 그게 다야.

key_expressions.note: 업무 맥락에서 'team sync' = 팀 짧은 미팅

key_expressions.ko: 마감 시간, 절대 넘길 수 없는 시간
key_expressions.note: 이후 일정이 있어서 반드시 끝내야 하는 시간
일정이 비어 있을 때. 'pretty free'와 유사

common_mistakes_ko: 'I can go' → 'I'm free' / 'I'm available' (참석 가능 표현)
'I must go out at 3:30' → 'I have a hard stop at three-thirty' (업무 표현)
'Sync'를 '동기화'로만 이해하면 안 됨 — 업무 맥락에서 '짧은 미팅' 의미

scenarios.context_ko: 친구 생일파티 초대를 수락하고 세부 사항 확인하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey! Did you get the invite for my birthday thing Saturday?
dialogue.ko: 야! 토요일 내 생일 파티 초대장 받았어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I did! I'm definitely coming. What time does it start?
dialogue.ko: 응, 받았어! 당연히 갈 거야. 몇 시에 시작해?
alt_en: Got it — I'll be there. What time are you starting?
Yes! Wouldn't miss it. When does it kick off?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Around seven. Pretty casual — just dinner and drinks at my place.
dialogue.ko: 7시쯤. 편하게 — 우리 집에서 저녁 먹고 술 마실 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sounds fun. Should I bring anything? Like, food or drinks?
dialogue.ko: 재미있겠다. 뭐 가져갈까? 음식이나 음료 같은 거?
alt_en: Perfect. Want me to bring something?
Nice — is there anything I should bring?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Just yourself, honestly. Though if you want to bring something to share, wine works.
dialogue.ko: 그냥 와. 솔직히. 뭔가 갖고 싶으면 와인이 괜찮아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'bring anything' → 'bring something to share'로 더 구체적인 공유 맥락으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'll bring a bottle. Red or white — any preference?
dialogue.ko: 한 병 가져갈게. 레드야 화이트야 — 선호하는 거 있어?
alt_en: I'll grab a bottle. Red or white?
Count on a bottle from me. Color preference?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Either's great. Can't wait to see you!
dialogue.ko: 둘 다 좋아. 빨리 보고 싶다!

key_expressions.ko: 절대 안 빠질게, 꼭 갈 거야
key_expressions.note: 강한 참석 의사 표현
손님에게 선물·음식 없어도 된다고 할 때
파티에 가져가는 공유용 음식·음료 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I will go' → 'I'm definitely coming' / 'Wouldn't miss it' (강한 참석 의사)
'Bring something?' → 'Should I bring anything?' (의문문 패턴 주의 — anything, not something)
'Red wine or white wine?' → 'Red or white?' (반복 단어 생략이 더 자연스럽다)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국 파티에서 'Just bring yourself'는 빈말이 아니라 진심인 경우가 많다. 하지만 와인 한 병 정도 가져가는 것이 일반적인 예의다.

scenarios.context_ko: 잡아둔 만남 장소를 더 편한 곳으로 바꾸자고 제안하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, would you mind if we changed where we're meeting? The traffic into downtown is rough today.
dialogue.ko: 야, 만나는 장소 바꿔도 돼? 오늘 시내로 가는 교통이 너무 막혀.
alt_en: Can we swap the meetup spot? Downtown traffic is a disaster.
Do you mind moving where we meet? Traffic is bad today.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh totally, no problem. Where were you thinking?
dialogue.ko: 아 물론이지, 괜찮아. 어디 생각해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: There's a café near my place. It's, uh, quiet and parking is easy.
dialogue.ko: 우리 집 근처에 카페 있어. 조용하고, 음, 주차도 쉬워.
alt_en: There's a café by me — easy parking, low-key vibe.
A place near my apartment. Quiet, easy to get to.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Easy parking sounds perfect. What's it called?
dialogue.ko: 주차 편하면 완전 좋지. 이름이 뭐야?
dialogue.recast_note: 'parking is easy' → 'easy parking' 도치로 강조하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Café Grain. It's right next to the post office on Maple Street.
dialogue.ko: 카페 그레인. 메이플 스트리트 우체국 바로 옆이야.
alt_en: Café Grain — next to the post office on Maple.
It's called Café Grain. Just off Maple Street.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Got it. I'll look it up. Still two o'clock?
dialogue.ko: 알겠어. 찾아볼게. 시간은 아직 2시야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, two o'clock is fine. See you there.
dialogue.ko: 응, 2시 맞아. 거기서 봐.
alt_en: Same time — two. See you!
Still two. I'll be there.

key_expressions.note: 변경·부탁 시 정중한 표현. 직접 'Can we?' 보다 부드럽다
swap = 교환·변경. meetup spot = 만남 장소
과하지 않고 조용한 공간 묘사

common_mistakes_ko: 'Can we change the place?' → 'Would you mind if we changed where we're meeting?' (더 공손한 표현)
'The traffic is very bad' → 'Traffic is rough / a disaster today' (강한 구어체 표현)
'Next to the post office' — 위치 설명 시 'right next to', 'just off' 같은 표현 적극 활용

scenarios.context_ko: 다른 부서 동료에게 자료 요청하는 짧은 이메일 형식 대화

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi, I hope this isn't a bad time. I'm working on the Q3 report and could use some numbers from your team.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 시간 괜찮으실 때 연락드립니다. Q3 보고서 작업 중인데 팀 수치가 필요해서요.
alt_en: Hi, I'm pulling together the Q3 report and need a few figures from your side.
Hope it's okay to reach out — I need some data from your team for Q3.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No problem. Which numbers are you looking for?
dialogue.ko: 문제없어요. 어떤 수치가 필요하세요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Specifically, the July and August sales figures. If you have them ready.
dialogue.ko: 구체적으로는 7월, 8월 매출 수치요. 준비된 게 있으시면요.
alt_en: The July and August sales data — if that's available.
Sales numbers for July and August, if they're ready.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I have them. When do you need them by?
dialogue.ko: 있어요. 언제까지 필요하세요?
dialogue.recast_note: 'If you have them ready' → 'I have them' + 마감 확인으로 자연스럽게 이어받으며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: End of day Thursday, if that's not too tight.
dialogue.ko: 목요일 업무 마감까지요, 너무 촉박하지 않으시면요.
alt_en: Thursday EOD if possible — no rush if that's tight.
By Thursday, close of business.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That works. I'll send them over tomorrow morning.
dialogue.ko: 괜찮아요. 내일 오전에 보내드릴게요.

key_expressions.note: 'need'보다 부드러운 요청 표현
직장 이메일 표준 마감 표현
문서·파일을 전달할 때 구어적 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I need numbers' → 'I could use some numbers' (요청을 부드럽게 표현)
'Until Thursday' → 'by Thursday' / 'end of day Thursday' (마감 기한 표현)
'I will send' → 'I'll send them over' (over 추가로 더 자연스러운 구어체)

scenarios.context_ko: 고객 서비스 담당자로서 불만 고객 전화를 받고 처리하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thank you for calling Apex Support. My name is Sumin. How can I help you today?
dialogue.ko: 에이펙스 고객센터입니다. 저는 수민입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
alt_en: Apex Support, this is Sumin. What can I help you with?
Thanks for calling Apex. Sumin speaking — how can I help?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Finally — I've been on hold for twenty minutes. I have an issue with my order.
dialogue.ko: 드디어 — 20분이나 기다렸어요. 주문에 문제가 있어요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm so sorry for the wait. I completely understand your frustration. What's the issue?
dialogue.ko: 오래 기다리셔서 정말 죄송합니다. 충분히 이해합니다. 어떤 문제인가요?
alt_en: I apologize for the hold time — completely understandable. Can you tell me what happened?
Sorry about the wait. I understand that's frustrating. What seems to be the issue?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I ordered the blue jacket a week ago. It arrived, but it's the wrong size.
dialogue.ko: 일주일 전에 파란 재킷 주문했는데요. 도착했는데 사이즈가 잘못 왔어요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I see — you received the wrong size. Let me pull up your order and get that sorted.
dialogue.ko: 알겠습니다 — 사이즈가 잘못 오셨군요. 주문 조회해서 바로 해결해드릴게요.
dialogue.recast_note: 'it's the wrong size' → 'received the wrong size'로 더 명확하게 확인하며 paraphrase
alt_en: Got it — wrong size arrived. Let me check your order right away.
I understand. You got the wrong size — let me pull that order up for you.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Thank you. I just want the right size, not a refund.
dialogue.ko: 감사해요. 환불 말고 그냥 맞는 사이즈를 받고 싶어요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Absolutely. I'll process an exchange right now. What's your order number?
dialogue.ko: 물론입니다. 지금 바로 교환 처리 해드릴게요. 주문 번호가 어떻게 되세요?
alt_en: No problem at all. I'll get an exchange started. Do you have your order number?
Of course — I'll set up the exchange. Can I get your order number?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Got it. You'll receive the correct size within three to five business days.
dialogue.ko: 확인했습니다. 영업일 기준 3~5일 내로 맞는 사이즈 받으실 거예요.
alt_en: All set — expect the correct size in three to five business days.
You're all taken care of. Correct size arriving in three to five business days.

key_expressions.note: 고객 서비스 표준 공감 표현
영국식이지만 미국에서도 쓰임. 'fix it'의 부드러운 표현
고객 서비스 맥락의 공식 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I understand' 단독보다 'I completely understand your frustration'처럼 구체적 공감이 더 효과적이다
'Wrong size came' → 'received the wrong size' / 'it arrived in the wrong size'
'Change it' → 'process an exchange' (고객 서비스 맥락의 적절한 표현)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국 고객 서비스에서는 문제 해결 전에 반드시 공감(empathy)을 먼저 표현한다. 'I understand your frustration'처럼 감정을 인정한 뒤 해결책으로 넘어가는 것이 표준이다.

scenarios.context_ko: 리셉션으로서 외부 전화 받고 담당자 연결하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Good morning, Apex Solutions. How may I direct your call?
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 에이펙스 솔루션입니다. 어디로 연결해드릴까요?
alt_en: Apex Solutions, good morning. Who are you looking to reach?
Good morning, Apex. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hi, I'm calling for someone in your sales department. I'm not sure who handles accounts.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 영업 부서에 연락하려고요. 어떤 분이 담당하는지 잘 몰라서요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Of course. Could I get your name and the company you're calling from?
dialogue.ko: 물론입니다. 성함과 회사명 알 수 있을까요?
alt_en: Sure — may I ask who's calling and what company you're with?
Absolutely. Can I get your name and organization?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It's David Park, from Greenfield Inc.
dialogue.ko: 그린필드 인크의 데이빗 박입니다.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thank you, Mr. Park. I'll connect you with our accounts team. One moment please.
dialogue.ko: 감사합니다, 박 부장님. 계정 담당 팀으로 연결해드릴게요. 잠시만 기다려주세요.
alt_en: Thanks, Mr. Park — let me transfer you to our accounts team. Please hold.
Got it — putting you through to accounts now. One moment.
dialogue.recast_note: 'calling for someone in sales' → 'accounts team'으로 더 정확한 부서명으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sure, thank you.
dialogue.ko: 네, 감사합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm going to put you on hold briefly. Thank you for your patience.
dialogue.ko: 잠시 대기로 전환해드릴게요. 기다려주셔서 감사합니다.
alt_en: I'll put you on a brief hold. Thank you for waiting.
Just a moment — I'll have you connected shortly.

key_expressions.en: How may I direct your call?
key_expressions.note: 전화 리셉션 표준 표현
전화 보류 표현
전화 연결 시 표준 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Wait please' → 'One moment please' / 'Please hold' (정중한 대기 표현)
'I will connect you' → 'I'll put you through to ~' / 'I'll connect you with ~' (전화 연결 표현)
상대방 이름을 'Mr./Ms. + 성'으로 부를 때 경칭 사용이 미국에서도 공식 전화에선 표준이다

scenarios.context_ko: 자료 요청 메일에 답장하면서 현황 공유하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi Jenna, thanks for reaching out. I have most of the data you need.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요 제나, 연락 주셔서 감사해요. 필요하신 데이터 대부분 있어요.
alt_en: Hey Jenna — got your message. I have most of what you need.
Hi Jenna, thanks for the note. I can get you most of those figures.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Great! Do you have the July numbers too?
dialogue.ko: 좋아요! 7월 수치도 있나요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: July I have, yes. August is still being finalized — I'd say by end of week.
dialogue.ko: 7월은 있어요. 8월은 아직 마무리 중이에요 — 이번 주 안에는 될 것 같아요.
alt_en: July's ready. August is still in review — should be done by Friday.
I have July. August is still getting wrapped up — end of this week, maybe.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The August data is still coming — that's fine. Can you send July now?
dialogue.ko: 8월 자료 아직 작업 중이군요 — 괜찮아요. 7월은 지금 보내주실 수 있어요?
dialogue.recast_note: 'still being finalized' → 'still coming' + 긍정적 수용으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Absolutely. I'll attach the July file to this reply. August to follow by Friday.
dialogue.ko: 물론이죠. 이 답장에 7월 파일 첨부할게요. 8월은 금요일까지 추가로 보낼게요.
alt_en: Yes — attaching July now. August will follow by Friday.
I'll send July in a moment. August by Friday at the latest.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Perfect. That gives us enough to start. Thanks!
dialogue.ko: 완벽해요. 시작하기엔 충분해요. 감사해요!

key_expressions.note: 이메일 시작 표준 표현
진행 중인 작업 상태 표현
업무 이메일에서 추가 자료를 나중에 보낼 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'Thank you for contacting' → 'Thanks for reaching out' (더 자연스러운 구어체 이메일 표현)
'I am still making' → 'still being finalized' (수동태 사용으로 더 자연스럽다)
'August will come later' → 'August to follow' / 'August coming Friday' (업무 이메일 간결 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 팀에 회의 리마인더 메시지 보내기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Quick reminder — we have the team sync at two today. Don't forget to bring your updates.
dialogue.ko: 빠른 공지 — 오늘 2시에 팀 미팅 있어요. 업데이트 사항 가져오는 거 잊지 마세요.
alt_en: Heads up — team sync is at two today. Bring any updates.
Just a reminder: team meeting at two. Come with your updates.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Got it, thanks for the heads-up. Is there an agenda or just open discussion?
dialogue.ko: 알겠어요, 알려줘서 감사해요. 안건 있어요, 아니면 자유 토론이에요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: There's a short agenda. I'll send it over before the meeting.
dialogue.ko: 짧은 안건이 있어요. 미팅 전에 보내드릴게요.
alt_en: There's an agenda — I'll share it beforehand.
Quick agenda, yes. I'll drop it in the chat before two.
dialogue.recast_note: 'agenda or just open discussion' → 'there's a short agenda'로 질문에 명확히 답하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Perfect. I'll be there.
dialogue.ko: 완벽해요. 참석할게요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Great. See you at two.
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 2시에 봐요.
alt_en: See you then.
Okay, two o'clock.

key_expressions.note: 짧은 알림 메시지 시작 표현
'advance notice'의 구어체
슬랙·카톡 등 채팅에 파일·메시지 공유할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'I inform you' → 'Quick reminder' / 'Heads up' (알림 표현)
'Is there agenda?' → 'Is there an agenda?' (가산명사 관사 필수)
'I will send before' → 'I'll send it over beforehand' / 'before the meeting' (시간 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 매니저에게 휴가 신청 이메일 대화

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi Sarah, I'd like to request some time off next month if that's okay.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요 사라, 다음 달에 연차를 신청하고 싶어서요.
alt_en: Hi Sarah — I'm hoping to take some vacation next month.
Hi Sarah, I wanted to request leave for next month.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sure, what dates are you thinking?
dialogue.ko: 물론이죠, 어떤 날짜로 생각하고 계세요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I was hoping for June 16th through the 20th. Five days total.
dialogue.ko: 6월 16일부터 20일까지 생각하고 있어요. 총 5일이요.
alt_en: June 16 to 20 — five working days.
The 16th through the 20th of June. Five days.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Let me check the team calendar. June 16 to 20 — any critical deadlines that week?
dialogue.ko: 팀 캘린더 확인해볼게요. 6월 16~20일 — 그 주에 중요한 마감이 있나요?
dialogue.recast_note: 'June 16th through the 20th' → 'June 16 to 20' + 마감 확인으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: No major deadlines. I'll make sure my work is handed off before I leave.
dialogue.ko: 큰 마감은 없어요. 떠나기 전에 업무 인수인계 확실히 해둘게요.
alt_en: Nothing critical that week. I'll wrap up and hand off before I go.
No big deadlines. I'll make sure coverage is sorted.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sounds good. I'll approve it. Enjoy your time off.
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 승인할게요. 잘 쉬고 오세요.

key_expressions.note: 공식 휴가 신청 표현
업무를 다른 사람에게 넘길 때
부재 중 업무 커버가 됐다는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to take a vacation leave' → 'I'd like to request some time off' (더 자연스러운 표현)
'From 16 to 20' → 'June 16th through the 20th' / '16 to 20' (기간 표현 방식)
'Hand over' vs 'hand off' — 둘 다 쓰지만 업무 인수인계는 'hand off'가 더 미국식

scenarios.context_ko: 한동안 답장하지 못한 것에 대해 사과하고 내용 처리하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hi Tom, apologies for the delayed response — it's been a hectic couple of weeks.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요 톰, 늦은 답장 죄송합니다 — 몇 주가 정말 바빴어요.
alt_en: Hi Tom, sorry for the slow reply — things have been crazy on my end.
Tom, apologies for not getting back sooner. It's been nonstop.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No worries — I figured you were busy. Did you get a chance to review my proposal?
dialogue.ko: 괜찮아요 — 바쁘실 줄 알았어요. 제 제안서 검토해보셨나요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I did, actually. I went through it this morning. Overall it looks solid.
dialogue.ko: 했어요, 사실. 오늘 아침에 검토했어요. 전반적으로 탄탄해 보여요.
alt_en: Yes — I went through it this morning. Looks really strong.
I reviewed it today. Solid overall.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Great to hear. Any feedback or revisions you'd like to see?
dialogue.ko: 좋네요. 피드백이나 수정 요청 사항이 있으신가요?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Just a few small things on page three. The numbers in section two don't match the summary.
dialogue.ko: 3페이지에 작은 것들 몇 가지요. 2절 수치가 요약본이랑 안 맞아요.
alt_en: Minor issue on page three — the numbers in section two are off from the summary.
A small inconsistency on page three. Section two figures don't line up with the summary.
dialogue.recast_note: 'a few small things' → 구체적 위치 지정으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ah, good catch. I'll fix that today and resend.
dialogue.ko: 아, 잘 잡으셨네요. 오늘 수정해서 다시 보낼게요.

key_expressions.note: 이메일 사과 표현. 'late reply'와 유사
단순한 'busy'보다 혼란스럽고 바쁜 상태 강조
오류·문제를 찾아낸 것에 대한 칭찬

common_mistakes_ko: 'Sorry for late reply' → 'Apologies for the delayed response' (이메일 공식 표현)
'Very busy' → 'hectic' / 'nonstop' (바쁨의 강도를 표현하는 단어)
'It is wrong' → 'The numbers don't match' / 'don't line up' (불일치 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 팀원에게 화상회의 접속 방법과 준비 사항 안내하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, just sent the Zoom link for tomorrow's call. It's at ten a.m.
dialogue.ko: 야, 내일 화상통화 줌 링크 방금 보냈어. 오전 10시야.
alt_en: Heads up — Zoom link for tomorrow is in your inbox. Ten a.m.
Sent the meeting link — ten tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Got it. Do I need to do anything to prepare?
dialogue.ko: 알겠어. 준비할 게 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Just have your Q2 update ready. Five minutes max — it's a short check-in.
dialogue.ko: Q2 업데이트만 준비해줘. 최대 5분 — 짧은 체크인이야.
alt_en: Bring your Q2 numbers. It's a quick one — five minutes.
Just Q2 updates. Short check-in, five minutes tops.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Five minutes — got it. Is it just us or the full team?
dialogue.ko: 5분 — 알겠어. 우리만이야, 아니면 전체 팀?
dialogue.recast_note: 'five minutes max' → 'five minutes'로 축약하며 확인 후 추가 질문으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Full team. Seven people. So keep it tight and on point.
dialogue.ko: 전체 팀. 7명이야. 그러니까 간결하고 핵심만.
alt_en: Everyone — seven people. Stay concise.
Whole team, so keep it brief and focused.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Understood. I'll be ready.
dialogue.ko: 알겠어. 준비할게.

key_expressions.note: 정기적으로 진행 상황을 확인하는 짧은 미팅
시간·내용을 컴팩트하게 유지하라는 뜻
관련 있는 내용만 집중해서 말하기

common_mistakes_ko: 'Prepare something' → 'have ~ ready' (준비 표현)
'Only us or full team?' → 'Is it just us or the full team?' (질문 구조 주의)
'Keep it short' → 'Keep it tight' / 'keep it brief' (간결함 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 기대했던 일이 잘 안 풀려 친구에게 짜증 털어놓기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, you look annoyed. What's going on?
dialogue.ko: 야, 짜증 난 것 같은데. 무슨 일이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I didn't get the promotion. They gave it to someone who's been here like two years.
dialogue.ko: 승진 못 했어. 여기 온 지 2년밖에 안 된 사람한테 줬어.
alt_en: They passed me over for someone newer.
I got overlooked for the promotion. Two-year person got it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Seriously? After everything you put in this year?
dialogue.ko: 진짜? 올해 그렇게 열심히 했는데?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. Honestly, I'm more disappointed than angry. I really thought this was it.
dialogue.ko: 그러게. 솔직히 화나기보다 실망이 커. 진짜 이번엔 될 줄 알았어.
alt_en: It's more disappointment than anger, honestly.
I really thought I had it this time. More let down than mad.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Being let down after working that hard — that stings.
dialogue.ko: 그렇게 열심히 하고 실망하게 되면 — 진짜 아프지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'more disappointed than angry' → 'let down' + 'stings'로 감정을 더 강하게 표현하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. I just need to vent, I guess. I haven't told anyone else yet.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그냥 털어놓고 싶었어. 아직 아무한테도 말 안 했어.
alt_en: I needed to get it out. Haven't told anyone else.
Just needed to say it out loud. You're the first.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I'm glad you did. What are you thinking of doing — stay or look around?
dialogue.ko: 말해줘서 다행이야. 어떻게 할 생각이야 — 계속 다닐 거야, 아니면 알아볼 거야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I don't know yet. I need some time to think.
dialogue.ko: 아직 모르겠어. 시간이 좀 필요해.
alt_en: Haven't decided. I'll let it settle first.
Not sure. I need to sit with it a bit.

key_expressions.note: 인사에서 탈락·제외될 때
감정적으로 상처받을 때 쓰는 구어 표현
감정 발산 필요성 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I am more disappointed' → 'I'm more disappointed than angry' (비교 감정 표현)
'I want to tell someone' → 'I need to vent' (감정 털어놓기 표현)
'It hurts' → 'That stings' (더 구어적이고 강한 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 오랫동안 기다리던 좋은 소식을 친구에게 전하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh my gosh, I have to tell you something. I got into the program!
dialogue.ko: 세상에, 꼭 말해야 할 것 같아. 그 프로그램에 합격했어!
alt_en: You're not going to believe this — I got in!
I have news. I got accepted!

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No way! Which one — the design program?
dialogue.ko: 말도 안 돼! 어느 거야 — 디자인 프로그램?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yes! The one in Berlin. I can't believe it still. I've been trying for, like, two years.
dialogue.ko: 응! 베를린 거. 아직도 믿기지 않아. 2년 동안이나 도전했잖아.
alt_en: The Berlin one! I still can't process it. Two years of trying.
Yes — Berlin. Still in shock. I've been at this for two years.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Two years of trying and you finally got in — that is huge!
dialogue.ko: 2년 동안 도전해서 드디어 됐구나 — 정말 대단해!
dialogue.recast_note: 'trying for two years' → 'two years of trying' + 성취 강조로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know! I screamed when I saw the email. My neighbors probably heard.
dialogue.ko: 그러게! 이메일 보고 소리질렀어. 이웃들도 들었을 거야.
alt_en: I literally screamed. My whole building probably heard.
I saw the email and just lost it. Pure joy.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha! When do you leave?
dialogue.ko: 하! 언제 출발해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: September. So I have a few months. I'm terrified and excited at the same time.
dialogue.ko: 9월. 몇 달 남았어. 무섭고 설레고 동시에.
alt_en: September — I've got a bit of time. Nervous and thrilled all at once.
September. Excited and scared, honestly.

key_expressions.note: 기쁜 놀라움 표현. 'still'과 함께 쓰면 감동이 지속됨을 표현
중요하거나 인상적인 소식에 대한 반응

key_expressions.en: Terrified and excited at the same time
key_expressions.note: 상반된 감정의 공존 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I entered the program' → 'I got into the program' / 'I got accepted' (합격 표현)
'I cannot believe' → 'I can't believe it' (구어체에서 축약형이 더 자연스럽다)
'scary and exciting' → 'terrified and excited' (감정 형용사 어휘 선택)

scenarios.context_ko: 힘든 시간을 보내는 친구를 위로하는 대화

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey — I heard about your grandmother. I'm so sorry.
dialogue.ko: 야 — 할머니 소식 들었어. 정말 미안해.
alt_en: I heard about your grandmother. I'm really sorry.
So sorry about your grandmother.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Thanks. It's been... hard. She went pretty fast in the end.
dialogue.ko: 고마워. 힘들었어... 마지막에 너무 빨리 가셨어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I can only imagine. How are you holding up?
dialogue.ko: 얼마나 힘들지. 요즘 어때?
alt_en: I can't imagine. Are you doing okay?
That must have been so sudden. How are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Some days are okay. Others I just don't want to do anything.
dialogue.ko: 어떤 날은 괜찮아. 어떤 날은 그냥 아무것도 하기 싫어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That makes complete sense. Grief doesn't follow a schedule.
dialogue.ko: 그건 당연한 거야. 슬픔은 일정대로 오지 않잖아.
alt_en: That's totally understandable. There's no right way to grieve.
Of course. Everyone processes it differently.
dialogue.recast_note: 'some days okay, others not' → 'grief doesn't follow a schedule'로 감정 유형화하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah. I just miss her, you know?
dialogue.ko: 응. 그냥 보고 싶어, 있잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Of course you do. Is there anything I can do? Even just hanging out.
dialogue.ko: 당연하지. 내가 할 수 있는 게 있어? 그냥 같이 있어줘도 되고.
alt_en: I'm here if you need anything — even just company.
Let me know if there's anything at all. I can just come over.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Just knowing you're here helps. Thanks for checking in.
dialogue.ko: 네가 있다는 것만으로도 도움이 돼. 연락해줘서 고마워.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Always. Take your time.
dialogue.ko: 언제나. 천천히 해.
alt_en: Of course. No rush.
Anytime. I mean it.

key_expressions.note: 힘든 상황에서 상대방 안부를 묻는 배려 표현
슬픔의 개인차를 인정하는 위로 표현
상대방 상태를 확인하러 연락하는 행위

common_mistakes_ko: 'How are you?' → 'How are you holding up?' (힘든 상황에서 더 적절한 안부 표현)
'I understand' 보다 'I can only imagine' / 'That makes complete sense'가 위로에서 더 자연스럽다
'Contact me anytime' → 'I'm here if you need anything' (지원 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 친구에게 부탁했다가 거절당한 후 감정 처리하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I asked Mia to cover my shift Saturday and she said no. Just flat out no.
dialogue.ko: 미아한테 토요일 대타 부탁했는데 거절했어. 그냥 딱 잘라서 아니라고.
alt_en: Mia turned me down flat for Saturday.
I asked Mia about Saturday — she just said no.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ouch. Did she say why?
dialogue.ko: 아이고. 이유 말했어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: She said she already had plans. Which, you know, I get — but I was counting on her.
dialogue.ko: 이미 약속이 있다고. 뭐, 이해는 하는데 — 나는 믿고 있었잖아.
alt_en: Plans, apparently. I get it, but I'd counted on her.
She had something going on. Fair enough — but I needed her help.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You were counting on her and she turned it down — that's frustrating, even if it's understandable.
dialogue.ko: 믿었는데 거절하면 — 이해는 해도 답답하지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'counting on her' → 반복 + 'turned it down'으로 상황 재확인하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. I'm not mad, just a little, uh, let down.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 화나진 않는데, 그냥 좀, 음, 실망했어.
alt_en: Yeah — not angry, just a bit disappointed.
I understand why, but it still stings.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's fair. Did you find someone else?
dialogue.ko: 그건 당연한 거야. 다른 사람 찾았어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not yet. I'll have to ask around. I just needed to say it first.
dialogue.ko: 아직. 여러 명한테 물어봐야겠어. 일단 말하고 싶었어.
alt_en: Still looking. I'll reach out to a few people.
Haven't found anyone. Just needed to get it off my chest first.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good call. Try Jamie — she usually picks up shifts.
dialogue.ko: 그래. 제이미한테 물어봐 — 대타 자주 해.

key_expressions.note: 조건 없는 직접적 거절
상대방에 대한 기대·신뢰 표현
여러 곳에 문의할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'She refused' → 'She turned me down' / 'said flat out no' (거절 표현)
'I trusted her' → 'I was counting on her' (믿고 의지했다는 표현)
'Ask many people' → 'ask around' (여러 사람에게 물어보다)

scenarios.context_ko: 힘든 프로젝트를 마친 동료에게 진심 어린 칭찬 전하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey — heard the Seo project finally wrapped up.
dialogue.ko: 야 — 서 프로젝트 드디어 끝났다고 들었어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, just yesterday. It was a tough one, honestly.
dialogue.ko: 응, 어제 막 끝났어. 솔직히 쉽지 않았어.
alt_en: Finally. It was a grind, honestly.
Yes — wrapped up yesterday. Really challenging.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I could tell. You put in a lot of hours on that one.
dialogue.ko: 그렇게 보였어. 진짜 많이 했잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I did. More than I'd like to admit. But I think it turned out well.
dialogue.ko: 그랬어. 인정하고 싶지 않을 만큼. 근데 잘 된 것 같아.
alt_en: Way more than I planned. But the result was worth it.
Too many hours, honestly. But it came together well.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It turned out really well — the client loved the final presentation.
dialogue.ko: 진짜 잘 됐어 — 클라이언트가 최종 발표 엄청 좋아했잖아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'think it turned out well' → 'turned out really well' + 클라이언트 반응으로 확인하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh, really? I wasn't sure how they'd take it.
dialogue.ko: 오, 진짜? 어떻게 받아들일지 몰랐거든.
alt_en: That's a relief — I wasn't sure how it'd land.
Good to hear. I was a little nervous about their reaction.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: They were impressed. You should be proud.
dialogue.ko: 인상받았어. 자랑스러워도 돼.

key_expressions.en: Put in a lot of hours
key_expressions.note: 시간과 노력을 투자했다는 표현
결과를 평가할 때. 'come out'과 유사
상대방의 성취를 인정하는 칭찬 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'You worked very hard' → 'You put in a lot of hours' (노력 표현)
'The result was good' → 'It turned out really well' (결과 표현)
'Be proud of yourself' → 'You should be proud' (더 자연스러운 칭찬 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 뜻밖의 소식을 듣고 놀라움을 표현하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Did you hear? Jake and Lily are getting married.
dialogue.ko: 들었어? 제이크랑 릴리 결혼한대.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: What? Are you serious? They've only been dating for like six months.
dialogue.ko: 뭐? 진짜야? 사귄 지 6개월밖에 안 됐잖아.
alt_en: No way — they just started dating!
Seriously? That was fast.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I know, right? They announced it this morning.
dialogue.ko: 그러게, 맞지? 오늘 아침에 발표했어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm honestly shocked. I never saw that coming.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 충격이야. 전혀 예상 못 했어.
alt_en: I'm genuinely surprised. Didn't see that coming at all.
Wow. That came out of nowhere.
dialogue.recast_note: 'Are you serious?' → 'shocked' + 'never saw it coming'으로 놀라움 강도 높이며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Me neither! Are you happy for them?
dialogue.ko: 나도! 잘 됐다고 생각해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Of course — if they're happy, I'm happy. Just surprised.
dialogue.ko: 당연하지 — 두 사람이 행복하면 나도 행복해. 그냥 놀랐어.
alt_en: Absolutely. Good for them — just wasn't expecting it.
Yeah, happy for them. Just caught me off guard.

key_expressions.note: 완전히 예상 밖의 일에 대한 표현
예고 없이 갑자기 일어난 일
예상 못한 일에 준비 없이 마주했을 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'It's surprising' → 'I'm honestly shocked' / 'That came out of nowhere' (감정 표현 방식)
'I didn't expect' → 'I never saw that coming' (더 강한 표현)
'I'm happy for them' → 'Good for them' / 'Happy for them' (축하 표현 축약)

scenarios.context_ko: 지난 일에 대한 후회와 아쉬움을 친구에게 털어놓기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I keep thinking about that job offer I turned down two years ago.
dialogue.ko: 2년 전에 거절한 그 취업 제안이 계속 생각나.
alt_en: That job I said no to two years ago keeps coming back to me.
I can't stop thinking about the offer I passed on.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The one in Singapore?
dialogue.ko: 싱가포르 거?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. I was scared, so I said no. But, uh, lately I wonder if that was the right call.
dialogue.ko: 응. 무서워서 거절했거든. 근데, 음, 요즘은 그게 맞는 선택이었는지 모르겠어.
alt_en: Yeah. I chickened out. Lately I wonder if I made the right call.
Yes — fear got in the way. Now I'm not so sure it was smart.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What makes you think about it now?
dialogue.ko: 지금 왜 갑자기 생각해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: A friend from college just got a big promotion there. It reminded me.
dialogue.ko: 대학 친구가 거기서 큰 승진을 했어. 그게 떠오르게 했어.
alt_en: A college friend just got promoted there. It brought it back.
Someone I know is thriving in that role now. Makes you think.
dialogue.recast_note: 'lately I wonder' → 구체적 계기(친구 승진)로 후회의 원인 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I get it. But you made the best call you could with what you knew then.
dialogue.ko: 그 마음 알아. 근데 그때 알고 있는 것들로 최선의 결정을 한 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. It's just hard not to wonder 'what if.'
dialogue.ko: 알아. 그냥 '만약에' 하는 생각을 안 하기가 힘든 거야.
alt_en: Yeah, I know. Hard to shake the what-ifs though.
True. I just can't help playing it out in my head.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's natural. But you're doing well now. That matters.
dialogue.ko: 그건 자연스러운 거야. 근데 지금도 잘 하고 있잖아. 그게 중요해.

key_expressions.note: 기회·제안을 거절할 때
가정·후회의 핵심 표현
두려움 때문에 하지 못했을 때 구어 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Refuse the offer' → 'turn down the offer' (거절 구어 표현)
'I regret' → 'I wonder if that was the right call' (후회를 직접적으로 표현보다 의문 형태가 더 자연스럽다)
'What if' 뒤에 항상 가정법(had + p.p.)을 써야 함: 'What if I had taken it?'

scenarios.context_ko: 당황스러운 상황을 친구에게 털어놓으며 웃어넘기기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Okay, I have to tell you something embarrassing that happened today.
dialogue.ko: 있잖아, 오늘 창피한 일이 있었는데 꼭 말해야겠어.
alt_en: You're going to laugh — something embarrassing happened.
I need to tell someone this. It's mortifying.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh now I need to know. What happened?
dialogue.ko: 아 이제 꼭 들어야겠다. 뭔 일이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I waved at someone at a coffee shop because I thought it was my coworker. It wasn't.
dialogue.ko: 카페에서 내 동료인 줄 알고 손 흔들었어. 아니었어.
alt_en: I waved at a stranger thinking it was someone I knew.
I called out to someone at a café — totally wrong person.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh no — what did they do?
dialogue.ko: 아이고 — 그 사람은 어떻게 했어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: They looked at me like I was crazy. Then just waved back awkwardly. I, uh, turned around and left.
dialogue.ko: 미친 사람 보듯이 봤어. 그리고 그냥 어색하게 손 흔들어줬어. 나는, 음, 돌아서서 나왔어.
alt_en: They gave me this look and half-waved back. I just turned and walked out.
Made eye contact, waved back slowly... I spun around and left.
dialogue.recast_note: 'waved at someone' → 어색한 상호작용 전체를 'awkward half-wave' 장면으로 확장 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You just left? Without saying anything?
dialogue.ko: 그냥 나왔어? 아무 말도 없이?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: What was I supposed to say? I didn't even buy my coffee.
dialogue.ko: 뭐라고 해야 했어? 커피도 못 샀어.
alt_en: What could I say? I bailed without even ordering.
Nothing to say — I just bolted.

key_expressions.note: 'embarrassing'보다 훨씬 강한 당혹감 표현

key_expressions.en: They looked at me like I was crazy
key_expressions.note: 황당한 시선을 받았을 때 표현
상황에서 빠르게 도망가는 구어 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Very embarrassing' → 'mortifying' (강한 당혹감 표현)
'I went away' → 'I turned around and left' / 'I bolted' (자리를 피하다)
'Strange look' → 'looked at me like I was crazy' (시선 표현 방식)

scenarios.context_ko: 외국 친구에게 가족 구성원 소개하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Tell me about your family. Are you close with them?
dialogue.ko: 가족 얘기 해줘. 가족이랑 가깝게 지내?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Pretty close, yeah. It's just my parents and one older brother.
dialogue.ko: 꽤 가깝게 지내, 응. 부모님이랑 오빠 한 명이야.
alt_en: Fairly close — parents and one older brother.
Yeah. Small family — just my parents and an older brother.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh nice. How old is your brother?
dialogue.ko: 좋겠다. 오빠 몇 살이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: He's thirty-four. He lives in Busan with his wife and, uh, a baby that's like eight months.
dialogue.ko: 34살이야. 부산에 아내랑 살고, 음, 8개월짜리 아기도 있어.
alt_en: He's 34. He's in Busan with his wife and a newborn.
Thirty-four. Lives in Busan — just had a baby.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: So you're an aunt now! Do you get to see them often?
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이모구나! 자주 봐?
dialogue.recast_note: 'a baby' → 'aunt now'로 관계 변화를 강조하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not as often as I'd like. Busan is a few hours by train.
dialogue.ko: 생각만큼 자주는 아니야. 기차로 몇 시간 거리야.
alt_en: Less than I'd like — it's a few hours on the KTX.
Not often enough. The distance makes it hard.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's tough. Do you all try to get together for holidays?
dialogue.ko: 힘들겠다. 명절 때는 같이 모여?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Chuseok and Lunar New Year, usually. Those are kind of non-negotiable.
dialogue.ko: 추석이랑 설날은 보통. 그건 거의 필수야.
alt_en: We meet for Chuseok and Seollal, mostly. Family constants.
Usually Chuseok and Lunar New Year — those we never miss.

key_expressions.en: Not as often as I'd like
key_expressions.note: 원하는 빈도보다 적을 때의 자연스러운 표현
반드시 해야 하는 것. 가족 행사에 캐주얼하게 사용
가족·친구 모임 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I meet them sometimes' → 'Not as often as I'd like' (빈도 표현 방식)
'My nephew/niece' 대신 'I'm an aunt/uncle' 형태로 관계 표현하는 게 더 자연스럽다
'We must go' → 'It's non-negotiable' (필수 행사 표현)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 외국인에게 추석·설날을 설명할 때 'Chuseok' / 'Lunar New Year'라고 하면 대부분 알아듣는다. 'Korean Thanksgiving'은 추석을 설명하는 보조 표현으로 쓸 수 있다.

scenarios.context_ko: 친구에게 결혼 생활의 현실적인 부분 솔직하게 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: So how's married life? You've been at it for what, two years now?
dialogue.ko: 결혼 생활 어때? 벌써 2년 됐지?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, just over two. It's good, honestly. Different from what I expected though.
dialogue.ko: 응, 2년 조금 넘었어. 좋아, 솔직히. 근데 생각했던 것과는 좀 달라.
alt_en: Just over two years. Good overall, but not what I imagined.
Two years and change — better in some ways, harder in others.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: How so? Different in what way?
dialogue.ko: 어떻게? 어떤 면에서 달라?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Like, the small stuff adds up. Whose turn it is to cook, scheduling, all that. It takes, uh, actual negotiation.
dialogue.ko: 뭔가 작은 게 쌓여. 누가 요리할 차례인지, 일정 조율, 다 그런 거. 실제로, 음, 협의가 필요해.
alt_en: The daily logistics — cooking, schedules, money. It takes real effort.
It's the small things. Whose turn to cook, splitting errands — real negotiation.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The small stuff requiring real negotiation — that's what a lot of couples don't talk about.
dialogue.ko: 작은 것도 협의가 필요하다는 게 — 많은 커플이 얘기 안 하는 부분이야.
dialogue.recast_note: 'small stuff adds up' + 'actual negotiation' → 'small stuff requiring real negotiation'으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. But we've gotten better at it. You kind of learn each other's rhythm.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 근데 점점 잘 하게 됐어. 서로의 패턴을 배우는 것 같아.
alt_en: True. We've figured out a rhythm though.
Yeah. It just takes time to figure out how you both work.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's a healthy way to put it.
dialogue.ko: 그렇게 보는 게 건강한 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I think so. It's work, but it's worth it.
dialogue.ko: 그런 것 같아. 노력이 필요하지만 그만한 가치가 있어.
alt_en: We think so. Hard work, but we're in it together.
Yeah — effort, but worth every bit.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good answer. You both sound solid.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 대답이야. 둘이 탄탄하게 잘 하는 것 같아.

key_expressions.note: 사소한 것들의 누적 효과 표현
함께 생활하며 맞춰가는 과정 표현
긍정적 평가와 현실 인식의 균형

common_mistakes_ko: 'Married life is good' 수준의 단순 평가보다 구체적 에피소드(cooking schedule 등)를 함께 말하면 더 자연스럽다
'Negotiate' 동사를 어색하게 사용 — 'actual negotiation', 'takes negotiation' 명사형이 더 자연스럽다
'We learned each other' → 'We learned each other's rhythm' (리듬·패턴 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 반려동물 이야기로 시작해 일상적인 대화 나누기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: We got a puppy last week. His name is Mochi.
dialogue.ko: 지난주에 강아지 입양했어. 이름은 모찌야.
alt_en: We just adopted a puppy — Mochi.
We got a dog last week. Name's Mochi.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh my gosh, a puppy! What kind?
dialogue.ko: 세상에, 강아지! 어떤 종이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: A mix. We think part corgi, part something else. Still figuring that out.
dialogue.ko: 믹스야. 부분 코기, 나머지는 다른 종인 것 같아. 아직 파악 중이야.
alt_en: Mixed breed — some corgi, we think. Vet isn't sure.
We think he's part corgi. The rest is a mystery.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: A mystery corgi mix — those are usually adorable. How's the training going?
dialogue.ko: 미스터리 코기 믹스 — 그런 애들 보통 너무 귀여워. 훈련은 어때?
dialogue.recast_note: 'part corgi, part something' → 'mystery corgi mix'로 재미있게 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Slow. He understands 'sit' but everything else is, uh, a work in progress.
dialogue.ko: 느려. '앉아'는 알아듣는데 나머지는, 음, 아직 진행 중이야.
alt_en: Hit or miss. 'Sit' he gets. Everything else — not yet.
Early days. 'Sit' is solid. Beyond that, we're getting there.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's basically all puppies. Is he sleeping through the night yet?
dialogue.ko: 강아지 다 그래. 밤에는 잘 자?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Getting better. First week was rough — up every two hours.
dialogue.ko: 나아지고 있어. 첫 주는 힘들었어 — 두 시간마다 일어났어.
alt_en: He's improving. First week was like having a newborn.
Better now. First few nights were brutal — up constantly.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Like having a baby! Send me photos sometime.
dialogue.ko: 아기 키우는 것 같네! 사진 좀 보내줘.

key_expressions.note: 아직 완성되지 않았지만 나아지고 있다는 표현
아기·반려동물 수면 관련 표현

key_expressions.ko: 될 때도 있고 안 될 때도 있다
key_expressions.note: 결과가 일관되지 않을 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'He knows sit' → 'He understands sit' / 'He's got sit down' (훈련 결과 표현)
'Work in progress' — 단독으로 쓰거나 'a work in progress'로 쓴다
'Wake up in the night' → 'sleeping through the night' (밤잠 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 새로운 친구에게 절친을 소개하듯 묘사하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You mentioned your friend Hana earlier. You two seem close.
dialogue.ko: 아까 하나 친구 얘기 했잖아. 둘이 많이 친한 것 같던데.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, she's probably my closest friend. We've known each other since university.
dialogue.ko: 응, 아마 제일 친한 친구야. 대학 때부터 알았어.
alt_en: Definitely. We go back to university.
She's my closest. We've been friends since college.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's a long time. What's she like?
dialogue.ko: 오래됐네. 어떤 사람이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: She's super direct. Like, she'll tell you the truth even if you, uh, don't want to hear it.
dialogue.ko: 진짜 직설적이야. 뭐랄까, 듣기 싫어도, 음, 진실을 말해줘.
alt_en: Very straightforward — tells you what she thinks, no filter.
She's direct. Won't sugarcoat anything.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: She doesn't sugarcoat — those are the best friends to have.
dialogue.ko: 돌려 말하지 않는구나 — 그런 친구가 최고지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'tell you the truth even if you don't want to hear it' → 'doesn't sugarcoat'로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. She once told me a presentation I gave was terrible. She was right.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 한번은 내 발표가 별로였다고 했어. 맞는 말이었어.
alt_en: Totally. She once told me my pitch was weak. She was spot on.
Yeah. She told me flat out that my idea had problems. She was right.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha — sounds like someone you want in your corner.
dialogue.ko: 하 — 내 편에 있으면 좋은 사람이네.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Always. She's the first person I call when I have a big decision.
dialogue.ko: 항상. 큰 결정이 있을 때 제일 먼저 전화하는 사람이야.
alt_en: Without a doubt. She's my first call for anything important.
Exactly — she's my go-to for anything major.

key_expressions.note: 사실을 부드럽게 포장하다. 'doesn't sugarcoat' = 솔직하다
권투에서 유래. 내 편에 있어준다는 표현
특정 상황에서 믿고 찾는 사람

common_mistakes_ko: 'She is a very honest person' → 'She doesn't sugarcoat' (특성을 더 생생하게 표현)
'She is in my side' → 'She's in my corner' (편을 들어준다는 표현)
'The person I call first' → 'My first call' / 'My go-to' (간결한 구어체 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 어린 시절 재미있는 추억을 친구에게 들려주기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I was going through some old photos and found this picture of me from elementary school.
dialogue.ko: 오래된 사진 정리하다가 초등학교 때 사진 찾았어.
alt_en: Found this old photo of myself from elementary school.
I was sorting through old pictures and stumbled on this one from grade school.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh show me! What were you like back then?
dialogue.ko: 아 보여줘! 그때 어떤 아이였어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Very shy. I wouldn't even raise my hand in class. And I had the worst haircut.
dialogue.ko: 엄청 소심했어. 수업에서 손도 못 들었어. 그리고 헤어스타일이 최악이었어.
alt_en: Really shy. Hardly talked. And the hair was something else.
So quiet — never raised my hand. And the haircut... let's not.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Shy and a bad haircut — we all had that era. What changed?
dialogue.ko: 소심하고 헤어스타일까지 — 다 그런 시기가 있지. 뭐가 달라진 거야?
dialogue.recast_note: 'very shy' + 'worst haircut' → 'shy and a bad haircut'으로 묶어 요약하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Middle school, I think. I joined a theater club and just kind of came out of my shell.
dialogue.ko: 중학교인 것 같아. 연극 동아리 들어가고 나서 자연스럽게 껍데기가 벗겨졌어.
alt_en: Middle school drama club. That changed everything.
I joined theater in middle school and just sort of opened up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Theater — that tracks. You're so comfortable talking now.
dialogue.ko: 연극이구나 — 딱 맞는 것 같아. 지금 말하는 거 엄청 편해 보이잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ha. Still working on it, honestly. But yeah, way better than before.
dialogue.ko: 하. 솔직히 아직도 노력 중이야. 근데 맞아, 예전보단 훨씬 나아.
alt_en: Still a work in progress, honestly. But yeah, so much better.
Ha — I have my moments. But miles ahead of who I was.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Growth. Love to see it.
dialogue.ko: 성장이야. 보기 좋다.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thanks. The photo on the other hand — that stays hidden.
dialogue.ko: 고마워. 그 사진은 반대로 — 그냥 묻어둬야겠어.
alt_en: Thanks. The photo though — that one's going back in the box.
Appreciate that. The picture is another story.

key_expressions.note: 내성적인 사람이 활발해지는 표현
정보가 이전 것과 일치할 때 쓰는 구어 표현
완전하지 않지만 개선 중임을 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I became more open' → 'came out of my shell' (성격 변화 표현)
'That makes sense' → 'That tracks' (더 구어적인 납득 표현)
'I am still learning' → 'Still working on it' (진행 중 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 외국 친구에게 추석 명절 분위기와 가족 행사 설명하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You mentioned Chuseok is coming up. What's it like for your family?
dialogue.ko: 추석이 다가온다고 했잖아. 너네 가족은 어때?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: It's pretty big for us. Everyone comes home — grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins.
dialogue.ko: 우리한테는 꽤 큰 행사야. 다 집에 와 — 할아버지 할머니, 이모, 삼촌, 사촌들.
alt_en: It's a big deal. The whole extended family gathers at my grandparents' place.
Very significant for us — whole family reunites.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The whole extended family — sounds like Thanksgiving!
dialogue.ko: 친척이 다 모이는구나 — 추수감사절 같다!
dialogue.recast_note: 'everyone comes home' → 'whole extended family' + 추수감사절 비유로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Kind of, yeah. There's a lot of food — especially songpyeon, which are these rice cakes.
dialogue.ko: 비슷해, 맞아. 음식이 엄청 많아 — 특히 송편, 쌀떡이야.
alt_en: Similar. Lots of food — songpyeon being the main one, rice cake dumplings.
Yeah. Tons of food — songpyeon, these traditional rice cakes, are the centerpiece.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: And do you make them together?
dialogue.ko: 다 같이 만들어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Usually yes. The kids help shape them. It's, uh, kind of a tradition we've kept up.
dialogue.ko: 보통 그래. 아이들이 모양 만드는 거 도와. 우리가 유지해온, 음, 전통 같은 거야.
alt_en: Usually. The kids help shape them — it's a tradition we hold onto.
We do. Kids shape the rice cakes — been doing it forever.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's such a nice tradition to pass down. Do you all stay at one house?
dialogue.ko: 전통을 이어가는 거 너무 좋다. 다 한 집에서 자?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, my grandparents' house. It gets crowded, but that's part of it.
dialogue.ko: 응, 할아버지 할머니 댁에. 좁아지는데, 그게 또 일부야.
alt_en: Grandparents' place — packed, but that's half the fun.
Yes, grandparents' house. Cramped but in a good way.

key_expressions.note: 부모·형제 외 조부모·친척 포함한 가족 전체
관습·전통을 지속하는 표현
상황의 불편함도 경험의 일부임을 인정

common_mistakes_ko: 'All family' → 'the whole extended family' (가산명사 관사 + extended 추가)
'We make together' → 'We make them together' (목적어 them 필요)
'Part of the experience' → 'part of it' (불편함도 경험의 일부로 받아들이는 표현)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 외국인에게 송편을 설명할 때 'rice cake'만으로 충분하지만, 'filled rice cake dumplings shaped like a half-moon'이라고 하면 더 구체적이다.

scenarios.context_ko: 부모님 건강 문제로 걱정이 되어 친한 친구에게 털어놓기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: My dad went to the doctor last week and they found something on the scan.
dialogue.ko: 아빠가 지난주에 병원 갔는데 검사에서 뭔가 나왔어.
alt_en: My dad had a scan last week — they found something.
Dad's test results came back and there was something there.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh no. Is he okay? Do you know what it is yet?
dialogue.ko: 아이고. 괜찮으셔? 뭔지는 알아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not yet. They want to do a follow-up next week. I'm, uh, trying not to panic.
dialogue.ko: 아직. 다음 주에 추가 검사 하자고 하더라고. 나는, 음, 패닉 안 하려고 노력 중이야.
alt_en: They're doing more tests next week. I'm trying to stay calm.
We don't know yet. Follow-up next week. I'm managing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Trying not to spiral is the right instinct — one step at a time.
dialogue.ko: 머릿속에서 최악의 상상을 안 하려는 게 맞는 거야 — 한 번에 한 단계씩.
dialogue.recast_note: 'trying not to panic' → 'trying not to spiral'로 더 강한 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. It's just hard to wait. He's trying to stay positive, which makes it harder somehow.
dialogue.ko: 알아. 기다리는 게 그냥 힘든 거야. 아빠는 긍정적이려고 하는데, 그게 오히려 더 힘들어.
alt_en: Waiting is the worst. And he's so calm about it, which is weirdly harder.
I know. He's being so positive. Somehow that's what gets me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That makes sense. You're absorbing the worry he won't show.
dialogue.ko: 그 마음 알아. 아빠가 안 드러내는 걱정을 네가 받아내고 있는 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. I haven't told my brother yet either. I don't know when the right time is.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 오빠한테도 아직 말 안 했어. 언제가 적절한 타이밍인지 모르겠어.
alt_en: Right. I haven't told my brother yet — not sure when.
Yeah. And I don't know how to bring it up with my brother.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Probably sooner than later. He'd want to know.
dialogue.ko: 아마 빨리 말할수록 좋을 것 같아. 알고 싶어 할 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You're right. I'll call him tonight.
dialogue.ko: 네 말이 맞아. 오늘 밤 전화할게.
alt_en: Yeah, I should. I'll call him tonight.
True. I'll reach out tonight.

key_expressions.note: 의료 맥락에서 추가로 진행되는 검사·진료
부정적 생각이 꼬리를 물고 커지는 상태
시간 지체 없이 처리하라는 권유 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Additional test' → 'follow-up' (의료 맥락에서 추가 검사)
'Don't think too much' → 'try not to spiral' (과도한 걱정 표현)
'Tell sooner' → 'sooner than later' / 'sooner rather than later'

scenarios.context_ko: 친한 친구와 싸운 후 화해를 시도하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I want to reach out to Jihoon, but I don't know how to start.
dialogue.ko: 지훈한테 먼저 연락하고 싶은데, 어떻게 시작해야 할지 모르겠어.
alt_en: I'm thinking of reaching out to Jihoon — not sure how to open it.
I want to make things right with Jihoon. Just don't know where to start.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: How long has it been since you two talked?
dialogue.ko: 마지막으로 말한 게 얼마나 됐어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Almost three weeks. I said something I, uh, shouldn't have. And I think it really hurt him.
dialogue.ko: 거의 3주. 내가 하지 말아야 할 말을 했어, 음. 그게 진짜 상처를 준 것 같아.
alt_en: Three weeks. I said something pretty bad. I think I hurt him.
Almost a month. I crossed a line and I know it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Three weeks after saying something that hurt him — that's a long time to let it sit.
dialogue.ko: 상처 줄 말 하고 3주가 지났구나 — 너무 오래 뒀네.
dialogue.recast_note: 'said something I shouldn't have' + 'hurt him' → 'said something that hurt him'으로 압축 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. I was embarrassed. But I miss him. He's one of my closest friends.
dialogue.ko: 알아. 창피해서. 근데 보고 싶어. 제일 친한 친구 중 하나야.
alt_en: I know — pride got in the way. But I miss him too much.
Yeah. I was too embarrassed. But he matters to me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Then lead with that. Not the argument — just that you miss him.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 그걸로 시작해. 싸운 얘기 말고 — 그냥 보고 싶다고.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's... actually simple. Do you think he'll respond?
dialogue.ko: 그게... 사실 간단하네. 그가 답장할 것 같아?
alt_en: That's a good angle. Think he'll respond?
Simple but hard. You think he'll reply?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Honestly? I don't know. But you won't know until you try.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히? 모르겠어. 근데 해보기 전까지는 모르지.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You're right. I'll text him tonight.
dialogue.ko: 네 말이 맞아. 오늘 밤 문자 보낼게.
alt_en: True. I'll reach out tonight.
Right. I'll send something tonight.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good. Let me know how it goes.
dialogue.ko: 잘 됐어. 어떻게 됐는지 알려줘.

key_expressions.note: 먼저 손을 내미는 연락 행동
상황을 해결하지 않고 방치하는 것
대화나 메시지를 특정 내용으로 시작하는 전략적 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Contact first' → 'reach out' (먼저 연락하는 표현)
'Leave it for a long time' → 'let it sit' (해결 안 하고 방치하다)
'Start with that' → 'lead with that' (대화 전략 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 새로 시작한 운동 취미를 친구에게 소개하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I've been getting into rock climbing lately. Like, indoors at first.
dialogue.ko: 요즘 암벽등반 빠졌어. 처음엔 실내로.
alt_en: I've started rock climbing — indoor gym first.
Been trying out climbing recently. Started inside.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, nice. Is it as hard as it looks?
dialogue.ko: 오, 좋겠다. 보기만큼 어려워?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: At first, yeah. My arms were, uh, wrecked after the first session.
dialogue.ko: 처음엔 그렇지. 첫 번 하고 나서 팔이, 음, 완전 망가졌어.
alt_en: The first few times, definitely. Arms were done after session one.
Harder than I thought. I could barely use my arms the next day.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Arms wrecked after one session — sounds about right. Do you go with anyone?
dialogue.ko: 첫 번에 팔이 망가지다니 — 그게 정상이지. 누구랑 같이 가?
dialogue.recast_note: 'arms were wrecked' → 'arms wrecked' 압축 + 동의로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: By myself, mostly. I like that I can go at my own pace.
dialogue.ko: 주로 혼자. 내 페이스대로 할 수 있어서 좋아.
alt_en: Solo mostly. I like setting my own pace.
I go alone. No pressure that way.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's a big draw for solo sports. Any goals?
dialogue.ko: 솔로 스포츠의 큰 매력이지. 목표 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I want to try outdoor climbing by end of year. Baby steps for now though.
dialogue.ko: 연말까지 야외 등반 도전해보고 싶어. 지금은 일단 조금씩.
alt_en: Outdoor by the end of the year, hopefully. Taking it slow for now.
Goal is outdoor climbing by December. Just building up.

key_expressions.note: 새로운 취미나 관심사를 시작할 때
남과 비교 없이 자신의 속도로 하는 것
천천히 조금씩 진행하는 접근 방식

common_mistakes_ko: 'I am interested in climbing' → 'I've been getting into climbing' (현재까지의 흐름 표현)
'My arms were very tired' → 'My arms were wrecked / done' (강한 피로 표현)
'Step by step' → 'baby steps' (조금씩 진행하다)

scenarios.context_ko: 최근 본 드라마 추천하면서 취향 대화 나누기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Have you watched anything good lately? I need something new.
dialogue.ko: 요즘 뭔가 볼 만한 거 봤어? 새로운 거 필요해.
alt_en: I need a new show. Seen anything worth watching?
What are you watching these days? I'm out of ideas.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh! I just finished this crime drama. Totally hooked from episode one.
dialogue.ko: 오! 범죄 드라마 방금 다 봤어. 1화부터 완전 빠졌어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Crime dramas aren't usually my thing, but I'm open. What's the premise?
dialogue.ko: 범죄 드라마는 보통 내 취향은 아닌데, 한번 들어볼게. 줄거리가 어때?
alt_en: Not usually my genre, but I'm listening. What's it about?
Crime's not my usual. What's the setup?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Detective trying to solve cold cases, but they're all connected. And the twist at episode four?
dialogue.ko: 형사가 미제 사건들 풀려는데, 다 연결돼 있어. 그리고 4화 반전?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Don't spoil it! Okay, you've, uh, convinced me. What's it called?
dialogue.ko: 스포 하지 마! 알겠어, 음, 설득됐어. 제목이 뭐야?
alt_en: Don't tell me! Okay, fine — what's it called?
Stop — you had me. What's the name?
dialogue.recast_note: 'twist at episode four' → 설득된 반응으로 학습자가 흥미를 보이며 paraphrase 역할 전환

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: 'Cold Files.' It's on the major streaming platforms.
dialogue.ko: '콜드 파일즈.' 주요 스트리밍에 다 있어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'll check it out this weekend. Fingers crossed it's worth the hype.
dialogue.ko: 이번 주말에 볼게. 기대만큼이길 바라면서.
alt_en: I'll try it this weekend. Hope it lives up.
Queuing it up now. Hope it delivers.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Trust me — it delivers. Text me after episode three.
dialogue.ko: 믿어봐 — 실망 안 시켜. 3화 보고 나서 문자해.

key_expressions.note: 관심 없거나 선호하지 않을 때 부드러운 표현
처음부터 중독된 상태 표현
소문이나 기대에 실제가 맞는지 볼 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'It's not my interest' → 'It's not my thing' (취향 표현)
'I was caught from episode one' → 'hooked from episode one' (중독 표현)
'It's worth it' vs 'it delivers' — 기대에 부응한다는 뉘앙스는 'delivers'가 더 강하다

scenarios.context_ko: 최근 요리에 빠진 이야기를 친구와 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What's that smell? Did you cook all this yourself?
dialogue.ko: 이 냄새 뭐야? 이거 다 직접 만든 거야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah! I've been getting into cooking lately. Tried a new pasta dish tonight.
dialogue.ko: 응! 요즘 요리에 빠졌어. 오늘은 새 파스타 해봤어.
alt_en: I made it — I've been really into cooking lately.
Yep. Cooking's become a thing for me recently. Pasta tonight.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It smells amazing. What's in it?
dialogue.ko: 냄새 대박인데. 뭐 들어갔어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Roasted garlic, lemon, and spinach. Pretty simple but, uh, it works.
dialogue.ko: 로스티드 갈릭, 레몬, 시금치. 꽤 간단한데, 음, 맛있어.
alt_en: Roasted garlic, lemon, spinach — simple but solid.
Not complicated — garlic, lemon, spinach. Comes together well.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Simple but it works — the best recipes are like that. How long did it take?
dialogue.ko: 간단하지만 맛있다 — 최고의 레시피가 다 그렇지. 얼마나 걸렸어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'simple but it works' → 정확히 반복 + 일반화로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: About twenty-five minutes. I used to think cooking was hard but it's mostly just, like, practice.
dialogue.ko: 한 25분. 요리가 어려운 줄 알았는데, 대부분 그냥, 뭐랄까, 연습이더라고.
alt_en: Twenty-five minutes. Once you practice it, it's less scary.
Not long — twenty-five minutes. It's mostly practice.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What do you want to try next?
dialogue.ko: 다음엔 뭐 해보고 싶어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Risotto. I keep putting it off because it sounds complicated.
dialogue.ko: 리소토. 복잡할 것 같아서 계속 미루고 있어.
alt_en: Risotto — been avoiding it because it sounds intimidating.
Risotto's next. Just been putting it off.

key_expressions.note: 새로운 취미로 요리를 시작했을 때
하기 싫거나 두려워서 계속 연기하는 것
방법·레시피가 실제로 통할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'I delay it' → 'I keep putting it off' (계속 미루는 표현)
'Simple but delicious' → 'simple but it works' (성공적인 결과 표현)
'Cooking is practice' → 'it's mostly just practice' (주로 연습이라는 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 최근 다녀온 여행 경험을 친구에게 짧게 들려주기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Welcome back! How was Lisbon?
dialogue.ko: 잘 왔어! 리스본 어땠어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Better than I expected, honestly. The city has this amazing, uh, energy.
dialogue.ko: 생각보다 훨씬 좋았어, 솔직히. 도시가 진짜, 음, 에너지가 있어.
alt_en: So much better than I expected. The city just has this vibe.
Incredible, honestly. The atmosphere is unlike anything.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Did you do the touristy stuff or go off the beaten path?
dialogue.ko: 관광지 다녔어, 아니면 덜 알려진 곳?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Both. Did the main sights on day one, then just wandered for the rest.
dialogue.ko: 둘 다. 첫날 주요 명소 보고, 나머지는 그냥 돌아다녔어.
alt_en: Mix of both — hit the highlights, then explored on my own.
Main spots first day, then I just walked wherever.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Wandering with no plan — that's when you find the best spots.
dialogue.ko: 계획 없이 돌아다니기 — 그게 최고의 장소를 발견하는 방법이지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'just wandered' → 'wandering with no plan'으로 의미 확장하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. Found this tiny bakery in an alley. Best pastry I've had in years.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 골목에서 작은 빵집 찾았어. 몇 년 만에 최고의 페이스트리.
alt_en: Right. Stumbled on this tiny bakery in a side street. Unreal.
Yes — found a hole-in-the-wall bakery. Best thing I ate all trip.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yes! That's the best thing about solo wandering. Would you go back?
dialogue.ko: 맞아! 혼자 돌아다니기의 최고 장점이지. 다시 갈 것 같아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: In a heartbeat. Maybe next fall.
dialogue.ko: 두말할 것도 없이. 아마 내년 가을에.
alt_en: Absolutely. Already thinking about next time.
Without hesitation — maybe autumn next year.

key_expressions.note: 관광 명소보다 알려지지 않은 곳을 탐방하는 것
찾으려 하지 않았는데 발견했을 때
주저 없이 즉각 할 의향이 있다는 강한 긍정

common_mistakes_ko: 'Go to not famous places' → 'go off the beaten path' (덜 알려진 곳 표현)
'I found accidentally' → 'stumbled on it' (우연한 발견 표현)
'Of course' → 'In a heartbeat' (강한 즉각적 동의 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 독서 습관에 대해 친구와 이야기하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What's that you're reading?
dialogue.ko: 뭐 읽어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: A book about habits. How small daily routines can change everything.
dialogue.ko: 습관에 관한 책. 작은 일상 루틴이 어떻게 모든 걸 바꾸는지.
alt_en: Book on habits — how small routines add up to big changes.
It's about building habits. Small changes, big results.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sounds like it could be preachy. Is it actually useful?
dialogue.ko: 교훈적일 것 같은데. 실제로 도움이 돼?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, actually. More practical than I expected. There's, uh, real science behind it.
dialogue.ko: 응, 진짜로. 생각보다 실용적이야. 뒤에, 음, 진짜 과학이 있어.
alt_en: Surprisingly useful — not preachy at all. Research-backed.
Actually yes. More actionable than it sounds.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Research-backed and practical — that's the combo you want in self-help.
dialogue.ko: 연구에 근거하고 실용적이라는 게 — 자기계발서에서 원하는 조합이지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'real science behind it' + 'practical' → 'research-backed and practical'로 압축 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. I've already started doing a five-minute journal in the morning because of it.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 이미 아침에 5분 일기 시작했어 덕분에.
alt_en: Right — I started a five-minute morning journal because of it.
Yeah, I've already adjusted my routine based on it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's impressive. I can never stick to journals.
dialogue.ko: 대단하다. 나는 일기를 절대 꾸준히 못 하겠어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Five minutes is the key. It's low enough that you can't say no.
dialogue.ko: 5분이 핵심이야. 거절하기 어려운 정도잖아.
alt_en: Five minutes makes it doable. Hard to say no to that.
The five-minute limit is what makes it stick.

key_expressions.note: 도덕적 가르침을 강요하는 느낌의 내용
과학적 연구로 뒷받침된
습관·계획을 지속하는 것

common_mistakes_ko: 'Too educational' → 'preachy' (과도하게 교훈적인 콘텐츠 표현)
'Based on research' → 'research-backed' (더 간결한 표현)
'Continue to do' → 'stick to it' (꾸준히 유지하다)

scenarios.context_ko: 최근 빠진 모바일 게임 이야기를 친구에게 털어놓기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Okay, I have a confession. I've been staying up till two a.m. playing this phone game.
dialogue.ko: 있잖아, 고백할 게 있어. 핸드폰 게임 때문에 새벽 2시까지 안 자고 있어.
alt_en: I have to admit — I'm addicted to this mobile game. Two a.m. sessions.
Confession: this app game is ruining my sleep schedule.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh no. Which one?
dialogue.ko: 아이고. 뭔데?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: It's this puzzle game. You match tiles and, uh, build a town. It sounds boring but it's addictive.
dialogue.ko: 퍼즐 게임이야. 타일 맞추고, 음, 마을 짓는 거야. 지루하게 들리지만 중독성이 있어.
alt_en: A puzzle city-builder. Sounds basic, but I can't stop.
Match tiles and build stuff. Stupid but addictive.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The 'sounds boring but addictive' ones are always the worst. Level?
dialogue.ko: 지루하게 들리지만 중독성 있는 게임이 최악이지. 레벨이 어떻게 돼?
dialogue.recast_note: 'sounds boring but it's addictive' → 반복 강조로 중독성 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Two hundred and something. I don't want to say exactly.
dialogue.ko: 200 몇 레벨. 정확히는 말하기 싫어.
alt_en: Over two hundred. I'd rather not say more than that.
Past 200. Let's leave it there.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha! That's deep in. Are you going to delete it?
dialogue.ko: 하! 완전 깊이 빠졌네. 삭제할 거야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Probably not. But I'm setting a ten p.m. cutoff starting tonight.
dialogue.ko: 아마 아닐 거야. 근데 오늘부터 밤 10시 마감 정할 거야.
alt_en: No — but I'm setting a hard stop at ten tonight.
Not deleting. Setting a curfew though — ten p.m.

key_expressions.note: 약간 민망한 사실을 털어놓을 때
취미나 게임에 많이 투자했을 때

key_expressions.ko: 마감 시간, 더 이상 안 하는 시간
key_expressions.note: 시간 제한을 두는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to confess' → 'I have a confession' (고백 표현)
'I played a lot' → 'I'm deep in' / 'Level 200-something' (구체적 표현)
'Stop time' → 'cutoff' / 'hard stop' (마감 시간 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 다녀온 콘서트 경험을 친구에게 들려주기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I just got back from the Coldplay concert. I'm still kind of buzzing.
dialogue.ko: 콜드플레이 콘서트 방금 돌아왔어. 아직도 흥분이 가시질 않아.
alt_en: Just got home from Coldplay. Still coming down from it.
Back from the concert — still on a high.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No way! I've always wanted to see them live. How was it?
dialogue.ko: 말도 안 돼! 항상 라이브로 보고 싶었는데. 어땠어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Honestly, one of the best nights of my life. The light show was, uh, completely insane.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히, 인생 최고의 밤 중 하나야. 라이트쇼가, 음, 완전 미쳤어.
alt_en: Honestly incredible. The light show alone was worth it.
One of the best nights ever. The visuals were unreal.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The light show alone — people say it's like nothing else.
dialogue.ko: 라이트쇼만으로 — 사람들이 비교 대상이 없다고 하잖아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'light show was insane' → 'the light show alone' 강조로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: It's true. And when they played Yellow, everyone in the stadium sang along.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그리고 '옐로우' 할 때 경기장 전체가 같이 노래했어.
alt_en: It really was. And Yellow — the whole crowd sang every word.
True. When Yellow came on, everyone just belted it out.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Goosebumps just hearing that. I need to go see them.
dialogue.ko: 그거 들으니까 소름 돋는다. 나도 가봐야 해.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: If they come around again, don't wait. Get the tickets the second they drop.
dialogue.ko: 다음에 오면 망설이지 마. 티켓 뜨는 순간 바로 사.
alt_en: If they tour again, go. Don't hesitate on tickets.
Don't think twice — buy the moment they're on sale.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good advice. You've convinced me.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 조언이야. 설득됐어.

key_expressions.note: 흥분·설렘이 지속되는 상태
공연·음악에 맞춰 따라 부르는 것
티켓 등이 출시되는 순간 즉시

common_mistakes_ko: 'I'm still excited' → 'still buzzing' (흥분 지속 상태 표현)
'All people sang together' → 'everyone sang along' (함께 노래하다)
'When the ticket comes out' → 'the second they drop / go on sale' (출시 순간)

scenarios.context_ko: 배워보고 싶은 새 기술이나 취미에 대해 이야기하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I've been thinking about learning pottery. Like, actually making things with my hands.
dialogue.ko: 도예 배울까 생각 중이야. 뭔가 손으로 직접 만드는 거.
alt_en: I want to try pottery — making things by hand.
I'm thinking of signing up for a pottery class.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, that's such a good idea. I've always thought it looked therapeutic.
dialogue.ko: 오, 완전 좋은 생각이다. 항상 치료 효과가 있을 것 같다고 생각했어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. Plus I spend so much time in front of a screen. I want something, uh, hands-on.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그리고 화면 앞에서 너무 많은 시간을 보내서. 뭔가, 음, 실질적인 걸 하고 싶어.
alt_en: Right. I need something offline and tactile.
Yes — and it gets me away from screens, which I need.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hands-on and offline — that's a legit reason. Have you found a class?
dialogue.ko: 실질적이고 오프라인 — 충분한 이유야. 클래스 찾아봤어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'hands-on' + 'screens' → 'hands-on and offline'으로 핵심을 묶어 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not yet. I found one studio but their beginner class is on Wednesdays, which is, like, tricky for me.
dialogue.ko: 아직. 한 스튜디오 찾았는데, 초급반이 수요일인데, 그게, 뭐랄까, 나한테 좀 애매해.
alt_en: Found a studio — the beginner slot's Wednesday, which is hard for me.
There's one, but their class falls on a day I'm usually busy.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Keep looking — a lot of places do weekend classes too.
dialogue.ko: 계속 찾아봐 — 주말 수업 하는 데도 많아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Good point. I'll check a few more. I just want to start before I talk myself out of it.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 말이야. 더 찾아볼게. 스스로 그만두기 전에 빨리 시작하고 싶어.
alt_en: True. I need to commit before I overthink it.
I'll look around. I want to sign up before I lose the motivation.

key_expressions.note: 이론보다 실제 활동 중심의 무언가
정신적으로 치유가 되는 활동 표현
이런저런 이유를 만들어 포기하게 되는 심리 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Using hands' → 'hands-on' (실질적인 활동 표현)
'It looks like it's good for mind' → 'it looks therapeutic' (심리적 안정 효과 표현)
'Before I stop myself' → 'before I talk myself out of it' (자기 설득으로 포기하는 것)

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 최근 본 영화에 대해 감상 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, did you see that new Marvel thing everyone's talking about?
dialogue.ko: 야, 요즘 다들 얘기하는 마블 신작 봤어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I watched it last weekend. I thought it was, uh, pretty decent.
dialogue.ko: 응, 지난 주말에 봤어. 꽤, 음, 괜찮더라.
alt_en: Saw it Friday. It was solid, actually.
I caught it last week — better than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Just decent? I loved it. The action in the second half was insane.
dialogue.ko: 그냥 괜찮아? 나는 완전 좋았는데. 후반부 액션 미쳤잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The action was great, but the story felt, like, really thin to me.
dialogue.ko: 액션은 좋았는데, 스토리가, 뭔가, 너무 얇은 것 같았어.
alt_en: Action was fun but the plot felt weak.
Great visuals, but the story didn't hold up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You think the plot was thin? I thought they set up the sequel pretty well.
dialogue.ko: 스토리가 얇다고? 나는 속편 복선 잘 깔았다고 생각했는데.
dialogue.recast_note: 'story felt thin' → 'plot was thin'으로 더 영화 비평 용어로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Maybe. I'm just not a huge fan of setup movies, you know?
dialogue.ko: 그럴 수도. 난 그냥 복선용 영화 별로 안 좋아해서, 있잖아.
alt_en: Fair — I just prefer movies that stand alone.
Could be. Setup films don't really do it for me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's fair. What kind of movies do you usually go for?
dialogue.ko: 그건 맞아. 넌 보통 어떤 영화 좋아해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thrillers, mostly. Or anything with a good twist ending.
dialogue.ko: 주로 스릴러. 아니면 반전 있는 거.
alt_en: I'm into thrillers and films with unexpected endings.
Thrillers are my thing — or movies with a twist.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh then you'd love Parasite if you haven't seen it.
dialogue.ko: 아 그럼 기생충 안 봤으면 완전 취향저격일 거야.

key_expressions.note: 영화 비평 표현. thin = 내용이 빈약한
프랜차이즈 영화 비평 용어
What do you go for? = 어떤 걸 좋아해?
