common_mistakes_ko: 'I thought it was good' 수준의 단순 평가보다 'the story felt thin', 'the acting was solid' 같은 구체적 표현을 써야 한다
'I don't like sequel movies' → 'I'm not a huge fan of setup movies' (부정 표현을 완화하는 방식)
'What movies do you like?' → 'What kind of movies do you go for?' (go for = 선호하다, 구어체)

scenarios.context_ko: 친구가 추천한 식당에 다녀온 후 솔직한 감상 전하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, I finally tried that ramen place you recommended.
dialogue.ko: 야, 드디어 네가 추천한 라멘집 가봤어.
alt_en: I checked out that ramen spot you mentioned.
So I went to that ramen place you told me about.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh yeah? How was it? You liked it?
dialogue.ko: 오 그래? 어땠어? 마음에 들었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The broth was really good. Uh, rich and not too salty.
dialogue.ko: 국물이 진짜 맛있더라. 음, 진하고 너무 짜지 않고.
alt_en: The soup base was excellent — deep but not overpowering.
Really good broth. Flavorful without being too salty.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Right? That broth is what makes it. What about the portion size?
dialogue.ko: 그치? 국물이 진짜 핵심이야. 양은 어떻더라?
dialogue.recast_note: 'broth was really good' → 'that broth is what makes it'으로 핵심 요소 강조하며 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Smaller than I expected, honestly. The noodles ran out fast.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 생각보다 양이 적었어. 면이 금방 없어졌어.
alt_en: Portion was a bit small for me.
I could've eaten more — runs out quick.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah, it's not huge. Did you add the extra noodles? It's like two bucks more.
dialogue.ko: 응, 많은 편은 아니야. 면 추가 했어? 한 2달러 더야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh, I didn't know that was an option. I'll do that next time.
dialogue.ko: 아, 그런 옵션 있는 줄 몰랐어. 다음엔 그렇게 해야겠다.
alt_en: No idea that was a thing — good to know.
Oh, I missed that. Definitely next time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Worth going back?
dialogue.ko: 또 갈 만해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Definitely. Maybe next Friday?
dialogue.ko: 당연하지. 다음 주 금요일 어때?
alt_en: For sure. Want to go together sometime?
Yeah — we should go next week.

key_expressions.note: 특정 요소가 전체를 결정한다는 표현
재방문 가치 묻기. 'Is it worth going back?' 축약
옵션·선택지를 몰랐을 때 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'The amount of noodles was small' → 'The portion size was small' / 'Portion was a bit small' (portion = 양·1인분)
'I will go again' → 'Worth going back' / 'I'd go back' (재방문 의사 표현)
'I didn't know there was option' → 'I didn't know that was an option' (that 필수)

scenarios.context_ko: 핸드폰 교체를 앞두고 친구에게 추천 부탁하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I need a new phone. Any recommendations? I'm so bad at this stuff.
dialogue.ko: 핸드폰 바꿔야 하는데. 추천해줄 수 있어? 이런 거 진짜 모르겠어.
alt_en: Help me pick a new phone — I have no idea where to start.
I'm thinking of upgrading. What would you get?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What do you mainly use your phone for? Camera, games, work?
dialogue.ko: 주로 뭐 하는 데 써? 카메라, 게임, 업무?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Camera mostly. I post a lot on Instagram, so, uh, photo quality is big for me.
dialogue.ko: 주로 카메라. 인스타 많이 하니까, 음, 사진 퀄리티가 중요해.
alt_en: Camera's the priority — I use Instagram a lot.
Mostly for photos. I want a really good camera.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Camera-first, got it. Budget? iPhone territory or Android?
dialogue.ko: 카메라 우선이구나. 예산은? 아이폰 쪽이야, 안드로이드야?
dialogue.recast_note: 'photo quality is big for me' → 'camera-first'으로 압축 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm open to both. Budget is around a thousand dollars, like, give or take.
dialogue.ko: 둘 다 상관없어. 예산은 천 달러 정도, 뭐, 어느 정도는.
alt_en: Either works. I'm thinking around a thousand.
No preference on brand — budget's roughly a grand.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: At that price, iPhone 16 or the Samsung S25. Both have insane cameras.
dialogue.ko: 그 가격대면 아이폰 16이나 삼성 S25. 둘 다 카메라 미쳐.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: What's the difference? I always forget which one takes better portrait shots.
dialogue.ko: 차이가 뭐야? 어떤 게 인물 사진 더 잘 찍는지 맨날 헷갈려.
alt_en: Which one's better for portraits?
How do they compare for portrait mode?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: iPhone edges out on skin tones. Samsung goes wider and more vivid. Depends on your style.
dialogue.ko: 아이폰이 피부톤은 좀 더 낫고. 삼성은 더 넓고 선명해. 취향 차이야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I think I prefer more natural. Maybe iPhone then?
dialogue.ko: 나는 자연스러운 게 더 좋은 것 같아. 그럼 아이폰?
alt_en: Natural tones sound better for me — leaning iPhone.
If it's more true-to-life, I'd go iPhone.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah, go for it. I'll send you a link to the model I'd get.
dialogue.ko: 응, 그래봐. 내가 살 것 같은 모델 링크 보내줄게.

key_expressions.note: 우선순위를 한 단어로 요약하는 방식
정확하지 않은 숫자 뒤에 쓰는 표현
비교에서 근소하게 우세할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'I am not good at this' → 'I'm so bad at this stuff' (stuff 추가로 더 구어체화)
'Which is better?' → 'What's the difference?' (차이를 묻는 더 자연스러운 표현)
'Natural color' → 'natural skin tones' / 'true-to-life colors' (사진 색감 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 헬스 vs 러닝, 각자의 운동 방식에 대해 의견 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, you look like you've been working out. Are you going to the gym?
dialogue.ko: 야, 운동한 것 같은데. 헬스장 다녀?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not really. I've been running outside. About four times a week.
dialogue.ko: 별로. 밖에서 뛰고 있어. 일주일에 한 네 번.
alt_en: I've switched to outdoor running — about four days a week.
I run outside now, roughly four times a week.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Four times? That's a lot. How far do you go?
dialogue.ko: 네 번? 많다. 얼마나 뛰어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Around five k each time. It's become kind of a habit, I think.
dialogue.ko: 매번 5킬로 정도. 습관이 된 것 같아.
alt_en: About 5K per session — it's routine now.
Five kilometers, usually. It just stuck.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It stuck as a habit — that's the hard part. I can never get consistent at the gym.
dialogue.ko: 습관이 자리 잡혔구나 — 그게 제일 어렵지. 나는 헬스장 꾸준히 못 하겠어.
dialogue.recast_note: 'become kind of a habit' → 'stuck as a habit'으로 더 자연스럽게 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Running is easier for me because I don't need to, you know, schedule it.
dialogue.ko: 달리기가 나한테 더 쉬워. 굳이, 있잖아, 일정 안 잡아도 되니까.
alt_en: Running's more flexible — no booking, no commute.
I like that running fits into any schedule.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Fair. But don't you miss the strength training? Running doesn't build muscle.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 근데 근력 운동 안 하면 아쉽지 않아? 달리기는 근육이 안 붙잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's true. I'm thinking of adding some bodyweight stuff at home.
dialogue.ko: 맞는 말이야. 집에서 맨몸 운동 좀 추가할까 생각 중이야.
alt_en: Good point — I've been thinking about mixing in bodyweight work.
Yeah, I want to add something at home. Maybe push-ups and core.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Smart. Even twenty minutes of that makes a difference.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 20분만 해도 달라.

key_expressions.note: stick → stuck. 어떤 것이 지속적으로 자리 잡을 때
규칙적으로 유지하는 것의 어려움 표현
pushup, squat 등 도구 없는 운동 총칭

common_mistakes_ko: 'I exercise running' → 'I've been running' / 'I run outside' (exercise는 동사로 단독 사용 가능하나 running과 함께 쓰지 않는다)
'Make habit' → 'It became a habit' / 'It stuck' (make a habit은 다른 의미)
'Muscle exercise' → 'strength training' / 'bodyweight exercise' (근력 운동 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 도시 생활과 시골 생활 중 어느 쪽이 더 나은지 의견 교환

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I've been thinking about moving somewhere quieter. The city's getting to me.
dialogue.ko: 좀 더 조용한 데로 이사할까 생각 중이야. 도시 생활이 지쳐가.
alt_en: I'm considering moving somewhere less hectic.
Big city life is wearing me out — I want out.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Quieter how? Suburbs or actually rural?
dialogue.ko: 얼마나 조용한 거야? 교외야, 진짜 시골이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Maybe somewhere like, uh, an hour outside the city. Not too far.
dialogue.ko: 뭔가 도시에서, 음, 한 시간 거리 정도. 너무 멀지 않은 곳.
alt_en: Somewhere an hour out — not remote, but quieter.
Hour or so from the city. Close enough to come back easily.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: An hour out is still doable. But what about your commute?
dialogue.ko: 한 시간 거리면 해볼 만하지. 근데 출퇴근은?
dialogue.recast_note: 'hour outside the city' → 'hour out' + 실현 가능성 언급으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I work from home most of the time now. So it's less of an issue.
dialogue.ko: 요즘은 주로 재택근무라서. 그 부분은 덜 문제야.
alt_en: Remote work makes it possible — I rarely commute.
I'm mostly WFH these days, so commuting's not a big deal.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That changes things. You'd actually enjoy it then — more space, lower rent.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 얘기가 다르지. 그러면 진짜 좋을 것 같아 — 공간도 넓고, 월세도 싸고.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. Though I'd miss having everything close by.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 근데 모든 게 가까이 있다는 게 그리울 것 같아.
alt_en: Yeah — though I'd miss the convenience.
True. I'd miss being walking distance from everything.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's the trade-off. No place has it all.
dialogue.ko: 그게 트레이드오프지. 다 갖춘 곳은 없잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I guess. Maybe I'll visit a few places first before deciding.
dialogue.ko: 그렇긴 해. 결정하기 전에 몇 군데 먼저 가봐야겠어.
alt_en: Right. I'll probably scout some towns before committing.
Makes sense. I'll check a few spots first.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good call. Let me know what you find.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 생각. 어떻게 됐는지 알려줘.

key_expressions.note: 장소나 상황이 부정적으로 영향을 미칠 때
새로운 정보로 상황이 바뀔 때 쓰는 표현
장단점을 맞바꾸는 관계 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'The city makes me tired' → 'The city's getting to me' (더 자연스러운 구어 표현)
'I live at home' vs 'I work from home' — 혼동 주의. 재택근무는 work from home
'Good idea' → 'Good call' (판단·결정을 칭찬할 때는 good call이 더 구어적)

scenarios.context_ko: 새 직장으로 출퇴근 방법을 고민 중인 동료에게 조언하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, how are you getting to the new office? You live far, right?
dialogue.ko: 새 사무실 어떻게 출근해? 멀리 살잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm not sure yet. I'm thinking about driving, but the parking situation looks bad.
dialogue.ko: 아직 모르겠어. 차 가져올까 생각 중인데, 주차 상황이 안 좋아 보여.
alt_en: Still figuring it out — parking downtown seems rough.
Driving maybe, but the parking fees are killing me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah, parking around there is a nightmare. What about the subway?
dialogue.ko: 맞아, 그쪽 주차는 진짜 힘들어. 지하철은?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: It's two transfers. That feels like, uh, a lot for every day.
dialogue.ko: 환승이 두 번이야. 매일 하기엔, 음, 좀 많은 것 같아.
alt_en: Two transfers daily — I'm not sure I can handle that.
The subway route has two changes. Feels like too much.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Two transfers every day does add up. Have you looked at the bus?
dialogue.ko: 매일 환승 두 번이면 피곤하지. 버스는 찾아봤어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'two transfers feels like a lot' → 'two transfers every day does add up'으로 반복 강조 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not yet. Does it go direct?
dialogue.ko: 아직. 직행 있어?
alt_en: No, I haven't. Is there a direct line?
Haven't checked. Any direct routes?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Line 7 goes direct. Takes about forty minutes, not bad.
dialogue.ko: 7번이 직행이야. 한 40분 걸리는데, 나쁘지 않아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That sounds much better. I'll look it up after work.
dialogue.ko: 그게 훨씬 낫겠다. 퇴근하고 찾아봐야겠어.
alt_en: Way better than two transfers. I'll check the schedule.
Oh, that could work. I'll look into it.

key_expressions.note: 상황이 매우 나쁠 때. 'nightmare' 단독 또는 'parking is a nightmare'
반복으로 부담이 커지는 상황
교통수단 직행 여부 묻기

common_mistakes_ko: 'The parking is very difficult' → 'Parking is a nightmare' (강한 구어 표현)
'Direct bus' → 'Does it go direct?' / 'Is there a direct route?' (직행 여부 확인 표현)
'Transfer two times' → 'two transfers' (명사형으로 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 친한 친구와 결혼·연애에 대한 솔직한 생각 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: So is it serious with you two, or still just dating?
dialogue.ko: 너네 둘이 진지한 거야, 아직 사귀는 거야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Still figuring it out. We like each other, but, um, neither of us wants to rush.
dialogue.ko: 아직 정리 중이야. 좋아하긴 하는데, 음, 둘 다 서두르고 싶지 않아서.
alt_en: We're taking it slow — both of us agree on that.
It's early still. We're on the same page about not rushing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's probably the smart move. How long have you been seeing each other?
dialogue.ko: 그게 현명한 것 같아. 얼마나 됐어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Three months. Long enough to feel real, I think, but not long enough to know.
dialogue.ko: 세 달. 진지하다는 건 느낄 만큼 됐는데, 확신하기엔 아직인 것 같아.
alt_en: Three months — past the honeymoon stage, but still early.
Three months. You know each other but you're still learning.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Three months is enough to know if it's working. Do you see a future with her?
dialogue.ko: 세 달이면 잘 맞는지는 알 수 있지. 미래가 보여?
dialogue.recast_note: 'three months' 반복 + 'feel real' → 'if it's working'으로 실질적 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Honestly, maybe. She's great. I just don't know if the timing is right.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히, 모르겠어. 좋은 사람이야. 근데 타이밍이 맞는지 모르겠어.
alt_en: I can see it going somewhere. But timing's the question.
She's great — I'm just not sure about timing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Timing never feels perfect, though. That's kind of the thing.
dialogue.ko: 그런데 타이밍은 완벽하게 느껴진 적이 없잖아. 그게 함정이지.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, you're probably right. I'm overthinking it.
dialogue.ko: 맞아, 아마 네 말이 맞아. 내가 너무 생각이 많은 거야.
alt_en: You're right — I need to stop analyzing it.
Yeah, I'm in my head too much.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sounds like it. Just go with it and see what happens.
dialogue.ko: 그런 것 같네. 그냥 흘러가는 대로 봐.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. I'll try.
dialogue.ko: 그래. 그렇게 해볼게.
alt_en: Right. I'll stop stressing about it.
Good advice. I'll ease up.

key_expressions.note: 관계·연애를 급하지 않게 발전시키는 표현
두 사람이 같은 입장일 때
과도하게 분석하거나 고민할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'We are dating seriously' → 'It's getting serious' / 'Is it serious?' (더 자연스러운 연애 표현)
'The timing is not good' → 'The timing isn't right' (timing + right 패턴)
'I think too much' → 'I'm overthinking it' (구어체 표현)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국에서는 관계 상태를 직접적으로 확인하는 'DTR (Defining The Relationship)' 대화가 일반적이다. '사귀는 거야?' 같은 질문을 직접 하는 것이 자연스럽다.

scenarios.context_ko: 최근 읽은 책이나 본 드라마 서로 추천하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I just finished The Bear on streaming. Have you seen it?
dialogue.ko: 방금 스트리밍으로 '더 베어' 다 봤어. 봤어?
alt_en: Just wrapped The Bear — you watched it?
I finished The Bear last night. Seen it yet?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yes! It's so intense. What did you think of the ending?
dialogue.ko: 응! 진짜 긴장감 넘치잖아. 결말 어떻게 봤어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The ending was, uh, unexpected. I didn't think they'd leave it open like that.
dialogue.ko: 결말이, 음, 예상 밖이었어. 그렇게 열린 결말로 끝낼 줄 몰랐어.
alt_en: I wasn't expecting that open ending.
Left a lot unresolved — didn't see that coming.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Right? The open ending got me too — season three can't come soon enough.
dialogue.ko: 그치? 열린 결말이 나도 답답했어 — 시즌 3 빨리 나왔으면.
dialogue.recast_note: 'leave it open' → 'open ending' + 시즌 3 기대감으로 자연스럽게 확장 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Totally. I'll need something to fill the gap. Any book recommendations?
dialogue.ko: 완전. 빈자리를 채울 게 필요해. 책 추천 있어?
alt_en: Same. I need something else to binge — books count too.
Yeah. Got any good book recs to tide me over?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: If you liked the food angle — Kitchen Confidential by Bourdain. It's basically nonfiction Bear.
dialogue.ko: 음식 쪽이 좋았으면 — 부르댕의 '키친 컨피덴셜'. 논픽션 더 베어야 거의.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh, I've heard of that. Is it a fast read?
dialogue.ko: 아, 들어본 적 있어. 빨리 읽혀?
alt_en: I've heard the name. Is it easy to get through?
Heard of it. Quick read or long haul?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Very. Reads like a good story, not like a memoir. I'll lend you my copy.
dialogue.ko: 완전. 회고록이 아니라 소설 읽는 것처럼 읽혀. 내 책 빌려줄게.

key_expressions.note: 끝난 시리즈·공백을 채울 콘텐츠 표현
기다림이 너무 길다는 강조 표현
가독성 높은 책 묘사

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to recommend a book' → 'Any book recommendations?' (추천 요청 표현)
'Is it easy to read?' → 'Is it a fast read?' (읽기 속도·난이도 묻기)
'I heard about it' → 'I've heard of it' / 'I've heard the name' (과거 인지 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 동료와 재택근무 확대 이슈에 대한 의견 나누기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Did you see the news? They're rolling back remote work at a lot of big companies again.
dialogue.ko: 뉴스 봤어? 대기업들이 또 재택근무 줄인다더라.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I saw that. Honestly, I'm not surprised — a lot of companies were already pushing for it.
dialogue.ko: 응, 봤어. 솔직히 놀랍지 않아 — 많은 회사들이 이미 밀어붙이고 있었잖아.
alt_en: I saw it. Not shocked — it's been building for a while.
Saw it. Felt inevitable honestly.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What do you think — is that a good move?
dialogue.ko: 어떻게 생각해 — 좋은 결정이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Mixed feelings. Working from home helps my focus, but I do miss the team energy.
dialogue.ko: 복잡해. 재택이 집중에는 도움이 되는데, 팀 분위기는 그리워.
alt_en: I'm torn — I focus better at home, but there's something about being in the office.
Hard to say. Remote works for me personally, but I see the collaboration side.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The team energy side — that's what companies keep saying too.
dialogue.ko: 팀 분위기 얘기 — 회사들도 계속 그 이야기 하잖아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'team energy' → 동일 표현 반복으로 강조하되, 회사 입장으로 확장 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sure, but that can be solved in other ways. Like, two days a week in the office.
dialogue.ko: 그건 그런데, 다른 방식으로 해결할 수 있잖아. 예를 들어, 주 2회 출근.
alt_en: True, but hybrid solves that — two or three days in-office.
That's fixable with a hybrid model though.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hybrid sounds nice, but our manager will never go for it.
dialogue.ko: 하이브리드 좋긴 한데, 우리 매니저는 절대 안 할걸.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I know. That's the frustrating part — no flexibility.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그게 답답한 거야 — 유연성이 없어.
alt_en: Exactly. The rigidity is what gets me.
I know — the one-size-fits-all approach is the problem.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: We're not going to agree on this one with management, I think.
dialogue.ko: 경영진이랑 이건 의견이 맞기 힘들 것 같아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Probably not. But it's good to talk about it, I guess.
dialogue.ko: 아마도. 그래도 얘기하는 건 좋은 것 같아.
alt_en: Not likely. At least we're on the same page about it.
True. We can commiserate at least.

key_expressions.note: 찬반이 공존할 때. 'I'm torn'과 유사
정책·제도를 이전 상태로 되돌릴 때

key_expressions.en: Go for it (won't go for it)
key_expressions.note: 'our manager won't go for it' = 매니저가 받아들이지 않을 것

common_mistakes_ko: 'I have complex feelings' → 'Mixed feelings' (구어체 표현)
'Roll back'을 '뒤로 굴리다'로 직역 금지 — '축소/철회하다' 의미
'The manager will not accept' → 'won't go for it' (구어 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 동료가 제안한 업무 방식에 정중하게 반대 의견 내기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I think we should just skip the weekly check-ins. They eat up so much time.
dialogue.ko: 주간 점검 회의 그냥 없애면 어떨까? 시간을 너무 잡아먹어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure I agree.
dialogue.ko: 무슨 말인지는 알겠는데, 동의하기가 어렵네.
alt_en: I get the frustration, but I'd push back on that.
I hear you, but I think we still need them.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Really? How come?
dialogue.ko: 그래? 왜?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: For me, the check-ins are when things actually get resolved. Without them, stuff just, uh, slips through.
dialogue.ko: 나는 점검 회의 때 실제로 문제들이 해결되거든. 없으면 그냥, 음, 놓치는 게 생겨.
alt_en: Check-ins are when blockers get cleared. Without them, things fall through the cracks.
They're the one time I find out what's stuck. If we cut them, things pile up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Fair, but what if we made them shorter? Like fifteen minutes instead of an hour?
dialogue.ko: 맞는 말이긴 한데, 짧게 하면 어때? 한 시간 대신 15분으로?
dialogue.recast_note: 'stuff slips through' → 절충안 제시로 문제를 인정하면서 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That I could get behind. Fifteen minutes, focused agenda — that would work.
dialogue.ko: 그건 동의할 수 있어. 15분, 명확한 안건 — 그러면 될 것 같아.
alt_en: That works for me. Keep it tight and on-topic.
I'd be okay with that — fifteen minutes max, strict agenda.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Exactly. Same goal, less time.
dialogue.ko: 그거야. 같은 목표, 시간은 줄이고.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Let's try it next week and see how it goes.
dialogue.ko: 다음 주에 해보고 어떤지 보자.
alt_en: We can pilot it next week.
Sounds good — let's test it and adjust.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Deal.
dialogue.ko: 좋아.

key_expressions.en: I see where you're coming from
key_expressions.note: 반대 전 상대방 관점 인정. 직접 'No'보다 부드럽다
조건부 동의. 완전 찬성과 다름
주의·관리 부족으로 일이 누락될 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'I disagree' 직접 표현 대신 'I see where you're coming from, but...' 패턴이 더 정중하다
'I can agree to that' → 'That I could get behind' (동의 표현 구어체)
'Things will be missed' → 'stuff slips through' / 'falls through the cracks' (구어적 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 사무실 출근길, 동료와 주말 근황 주고받기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey! You make it to the hike on Saturday?
dialogue.ko: 야! 토요일에 등산 갔어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I went. It was, uh, pretty hard but really nice.
dialogue.ko: 응, 갔어. 꽤 힘들었는데 진짜 좋았어.
alt_en: I did. Tiring, but worth it.
Yeah — tough climb, but the view was great.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Nice. What trail did you do?
dialogue.ko: 좋았겠다. 어느 코스로 갔어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Um, Bukhansan. We started early, like around six.
dialogue.ko: 음, 북한산. 일찍 출발했어, 거의 6시쯤.
alt_en: Bukhansan — left the trailhead at six.
We did Bukhansan. Early start, six a.m.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Six in the morning? You're dedicated. Worth the early start?
dialogue.ko: 오전 6시? 대단하다. 일찍 출발한 보람 있었어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'started early, like around six' → 'early start' + 시간 강조로 자연스럽게 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Definitely. The view from the top was amazing. No people yet.
dialogue.ko: 완전. 정상에서 보는 경치가 진짜 장관이었어. 사람도 없었고.
alt_en: Totally. Sunrise view with no crowd — perfect.
Oh yeah. Clear skies and almost nobody up there.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That sounds great. I keep saying I'll go, but...
dialogue.ko: 완전 좋겠다. 나도 가야지 가야지 하는데...

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You should come next time. We usually go once a month.
dialogue.ko: 다음에 같이 가자. 우리 보통 한 달에 한 번씩 가거든.
alt_en: Join us next month — we go pretty regularly.
Come along next time. We do it monthly.

key_expressions.note: 구어체. 'Did you go?'보다 더 자연스러운 확인 표현
worth + 명사구 패턴
실행 못 하는 의도 표현. 'but' 이후 자연스럽게 페이드

common_mistakes_ko: 'It was very nice'처럼 very를 남발하기보다 'really nice', 'pretty hard' 같이 정도 부사를 다양하게 써야 한다
'I went to hiking' → 'I went hiking' (go + 동명사, 전치사 to 없음)
'The view was amazing' 앞에 무조건 'very'를 넣으려는 습관 — 이미 strong adjective이므로 필요 없다
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국에서는 주말 근황 물을 때 'How was your weekend?'보다 구체적 행사를 언급하며 묻는 패턴이 더 자연스럽다. 'Did you make it to ~?' 형식이 그 예.

scenarios.context_ko: 오전 업무 중, 동료에게 점심 함께할지 물어보기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, you eating lunch around one today?
dialogue.ko: 야, 오늘 점심 1시쯤 먹어?
alt_en: You free for lunch around one?
Want to grab lunch at one?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah, probably. What did you have in mind?
dialogue.ko: 응, 아마. 어디 생각해둔 데 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I was thinking, um, the ramen place downstairs.
dialogue.ko: 음, 아래층 라멘집 어떨까 해서.
alt_en: Maybe the ramen spot on the first floor?
How about that ramen place below us?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, I've been meaning to try that place. Is it good?
dialogue.ko: 아, 거기 한번 가봐야지 했는데. 맛있어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'the ramen place downstairs' → 'that place' + 'I've been meaning to try'로 learner의 제안을 받아치며 자연스럽게 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I went last week. The tonkotsu is really good.
dialogue.ko: 응, 지난주에 갔는데. 돈코츠가 진짜 맛있어.
alt_en: I tried it last week — the broth is great.
Went last Friday. Definitely worth it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sold. Let's head out at one then.
dialogue.ko: OK. 그럼 1시에 나가자.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sounds good. I'll come get you.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 내가 데리러 갈게.
alt_en: Perfect — I'll swing by your desk.
Great, I'll come by at one.

key_expressions.en: What did you have in mind?
key_expressions.note: 제안 유도할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 질문 패턴

key_expressions.en: I've been meaning to try that place
key_expressions.note: 과거부터 갖고 있던 의도를 표현. present perfect continuous 패턴
동의·결정 표현. 'Sounds good'보다 더 구어적이고 캐주얼

common_mistakes_ko: 'I will go get you' → 'I'll come get you' (미국 구어체에서 come/go 방향 혼용하지 않음)
점심 제안 시 'Do you want to eat lunch together?' 대신 'You eating lunch around one?' 같은 직접적 표현이 더 자연스럽다
'Sold'를 '팔렸다'로 직역하면 안 됨 — 구어체로 '결정, 동의' 의미

scenarios.context_ko: 믿는 동료에게 새 프로젝트 배정에 대한 불만 털어놓기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ugh, I just found out I'm on the Henderson project.
dialogue.ko: 아, 나 방금 헨더슨 프로젝트에 배정됐다는 거 알았어.
alt_en: I just got assigned to Henderson. Can you believe it?
So apparently I'm on the Henderson project now.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh no. That one's been a mess since day one.
dialogue.ko: 아이고. 그 프로젝트 처음부터 엉망이었잖아.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. And nobody told me — I just, uh, saw it on the system.
dialogue.ko: 딱이야. 근데 아무도 말을 안 해줬어. 그냥, 음, 시스템에서 봤어.
alt_en: Right? And I had to find out through the portal.
I know. No heads-up — just saw it listed.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You found out through the system? That's not okay.
dialogue.ko: 시스템으로 알게 된 거야? 그건 좀 아니지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'saw it on the system' → 'found out through the system'으로 더 자연스러운 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. I want to say something to my manager, but I don't know how.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 매니저한테 말하고 싶은데, 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어.
alt_en: I feel like I should bring it up, but I'm not sure how.
I want to talk to my manager about it, but I don't know where to start.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: What's your biggest issue — the project itself or how you were told?
dialogue.ko: 제일 문제가 뭐야 — 프로젝트 자체야, 아니면 통보 방식이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Both, honestly. But mostly, I mean, not being told in advance.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 둘 다. 근데 주로, 뭐랄까, 미리 안 알려준 게.
alt_en: Honestly, both — but the no-notice part bothers me most.
Both, really. The surprise is what gets me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Then focus on that. Just say you'd prefer to be looped in earlier.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 그 부분에 집중해. 그냥 더 일찍 공유받고 싶다고 말하면 돼.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's a good way to put it. Thanks.
dialogue.ko: 그렇게 말하면 되겠다. 고마워.
alt_en: Good point. I'll try that.
Yeah, that's a cleaner way to say it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Good luck. Let me know how it goes.
dialogue.ko: 잘 돼야 할 텐데. 어떻게 됐는지 알려줘.

key_expressions.en: That's been a mess since day one
key_expressions.note: 프로젝트·상황 비판 표현. 'day one'은 처음부터
정보 공유 맥락. 'keep me in the loop'의 수동형

key_expressions.en: That's a good way to put it
key_expressions.note: 'put it'은 표현하다. 상대방 말을 인정할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'I want to speak to my manager' → 'I want to say something to my manager' / 'bring it up'이 더 자연스럽다
'I found in the system' → 'I found out through the system' (find out = 알게 되다, through = 경로 표현)
'Good luck' 뒤에 'to you'를 추가하는 경우가 많은데, 미국 구어에서는 'Good luck'만으로 충분하다
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국 직장에서는 프로젝트 배정 시 사전 통보(heads-up)를 기대하는 것이 일반적이다. 'I'd prefer to be looped in earlier'처럼 시스템이나 절차에 대한 개선 요청을 직접 표현해도 무례하지 않다.

scenarios.context_ko: 점심 시간, 동료와 상사 업무 방식에 대해 가볍게 불만 나누기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Can I vent for a second? David keeps changing the deadline.
dialogue.ko: 잠깐 푸념해도 돼? 데이빗이 계속 마감을 바꿔.
alt_en: Ugh, David moved the deadline again.
Is it just me or does David keep shifting things around?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Again? That's like the third time this month.
dialogue.ko: 또? 이번 달에만 세 번째 아니야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. And he never, uh, gives us any notice.
dialogue.ko: 딱이야. 그리고 절대로, 음, 미리 말을 안 해줘.
alt_en: Right, and always last minute.
Yeah, zero heads-up every single time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Zero heads-up — classic David. What did he change it to this time?
dialogue.ko: 사전 통보 제로 — 전형적인 데이빗이지. 이번엔 언제로 바뀐 거야?
dialogue.recast_note: 'never gives us any notice' → 'zero heads-up'으로 더 구어적 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Friday. It was supposed to be next Wednesday.
dialogue.ko: 금요일로. 다음 주 수요일이었는데.
alt_en: This Friday — pushed up from Wednesday.
Friday now. Was originally next week.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Friday? That's way too soon. How far along are you?
dialogue.ko: 금요일? 너무 빠른데. 얼마나 됐어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Maybe sixty percent. I'm going to have to work late.
dialogue.ko: 한 60%? 야근해야 할 것 같아.
alt_en: About halfway — maybe a little more.
Around sixty. Not going to make it without overtime.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Rough. You want to grab coffee after and decompress?
dialogue.ko: 힘들겠다. 나중에 커피 한잔 하면서 좀 풀까?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I'd like that. Thanks for listening.
dialogue.ko: 응, 좋아. 들어줘서 고마워.
alt_en: Definitely. Appreciate it.
That'd help. Thanks.

key_expressions.en: Can I vent for a second?
key_expressions.note: 불만·스트레스 털어놓기 전 쓰는 표현
구어체로 '미리 말도 없이'. 'No notice'보다 강한 표현
일 후 쉬거나 긴장 푸는 상황

common_mistakes_ko: 'How many percent done?' → 'How far along are you?' (진행률은 far along으로 묻는다)
'I need to work overtime' → 'I'm going to have to work late' (work late가 더 자연스러운 구어체)
상사 이름 앞에 'my boss'를 매번 붙이는 경향 — 이름만 써도 충분하고 더 자연스럽다

scenarios.context_ko: 사무실에서 동료의 승진 소식을 듣고 축하하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, I heard the news — congrats!
dialogue.ko: 야, 소식 들었어 — 축하해!

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh — you heard already? That was, uh, fast.
dialogue.ko: 어 — 벌써 들었어? 진짜, 음, 빠르다.
alt_en: Already? Word travels fast.
You heard? That just happened this morning.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sara texted the group. Senior manager — that's huge!
dialogue.ko: 사라가 단톡에 올렸어. 시니어 매니저 — 대박이다!

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm still surprised, honestly. I didn't think it would happen so soon.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 아직도 놀라워. 이렇게 빨리 될 줄 몰랐어.
alt_en: Still processing it, to be honest.
Honestly, I wasn't expecting it this early.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Are you kidding? You've been putting in the work. You earned it.
dialogue.ko: 무슨 소리야? 열심히 했잖아. 당연한 거야.
dialogue.recast_note: 'didn't think it would happen so soon' → 'you earned it'으로 learner의 겸손을 받아쳐 자연스럽게 반박

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thank you. That means a lot. Are you doing anything after work?
dialogue.ko: 고마워. 정말 힘이 돼. 오늘 퇴근 후에 뭐 해?
alt_en: Thanks, really. Want to celebrate after work?
That's so kind. Free for drinks later?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Nothing planned. You want to go out and celebrate?
dialogue.ko: 별 계획 없어. 나가서 축하할까?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yes, definitely. My treat.
dialogue.ko: 당연하지. 내가 살게.
alt_en: Absolutely — and it's on me.
Let's. First round's mine.

key_expressions.note: 소식이 빨리 퍼졌을 때 쓰는 자연스러운 표현

key_expressions.en: You've been putting in the work
key_expressions.note: 꾸준한 노력을 인정하는 표현. 'You worked hard'보다 구체적
지불 의사 표현. 'I'll pay'보다 더 캐주얼

common_mistakes_ko: 'It's my treat' → 'My treat' (주어 없이 쓰는 게 더 자연스럽다)
'Congratulate you' → 'Congrats!'/'Congratulations!' (자동사 형태로 직접 인사)
'I will buy' → 'My treat' / 'It's on me' (식사·음료 계산 제안 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 퇴근 후 팀 회식 제안을 정중하게 거절하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hey, the team's doing dinner at that Italian place tonight. You in?
dialogue.ko: 야, 오늘 팀이 이탈리안 식당 가는데. 올 거야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh, tonight? I actually have something going on.
dialogue.ko: 오, 오늘? 사실 오늘 뭐가 있어서.
alt_en: Tonight's tricky — I already made plans.
Ah, I wish I could. I've got something on.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ah, can't make it. No worries — what time are you done?
dialogue.ko: 아, 못 오는구나. 괜찮아 — 몇 시에 끝나?
dialogue.recast_note: 'I have something going on' → 'can't make it'으로 상황을 더 직접적으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Probably around eight or nine. Why?
dialogue.ko: 아마 8시나 9시쯤. 왜?
alt_en: Maybe around eight. What's up?
Eight or so. Why do you ask?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: We might grab drinks after. Could swing by if you're free.
dialogue.ko: 나중에 술 한잔 할 수도 있어. 시간 되면 합류해도 되고.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh, that works. I can probably join for drinks.
dialogue.ko: 오, 그거면 될 것 같아. 술자리는 합류할 수 있을 것 같아.
alt_en: Yeah, I could make the drinks part.
That might work — drinks I can do.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Perfect. I'll text you when we move.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 자리 옮길 때 문자 줄게.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sounds good. See you later then.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 그럼 이따 봐.
alt_en: Perfect. Text me.
Great, I'll keep my phone on.

key_expressions.note: 이유를 밝히지 않고 거절할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 표현
행사·모임에 참석 못할 때 표준 표현
가는 길에 잠깐 들를 때. 'drop by'와 비슷하나 더 캐주얼

common_mistakes_ko: 'I have a promise' → 'I have plans' / 'I have something going on' (선약은 'promise'가 아님)
'I cannot go' → 'I can't make it' (행사 불참 표현에서 더 자연스러운 구어체)
'After drinks' → 'for drinks' (목적 표현 시 전치사 선택)
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국에서는 팀 회식 거절 시 상세한 이유를 말하지 않아도 된다. 'I have something going on'으로 충분하며, 추가로 설명하면 오히려 어색할 수 있다.

scenarios.context_ko: 동료와 다가오는 휴가 계획에 대해 이야기하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I finally booked my vacation. Going to Jeju next month.
dialogue.ko: 드디어 휴가 예약했어. 다음 달에 제주 가.
alt_en: I just booked it — heading to Jeju in a few weeks.
Vacation's locked in. Jeju, next month.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh nice! How long are you going for?
dialogue.ko: 좋겠다! 얼마나 가?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Five days. I've never been, so I'm, uh, pretty excited.
dialogue.ko: 5일. 처음 가는 거라 꽤, 음, 설레.
alt_en: Five nights. First time, so I can't wait.
Five days — I've been wanting to go for a while.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Five days in Jeju — you'll love it. Any plans yet?
dialogue.ko: 제주 5일 — 너무 좋을 거야. 계획 있어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'Going to Jeju next month' / '5 days' 정보를 'Five days in Jeju'로 자연스럽게 통합 반복

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I want to rent a car and just drive around. Maybe hike Hallasan.
dialogue.ko: 응, 차 빌려서 그냥 드라이브하고 싶어. 한라산 등산도.
alt_en: Thinking of renting a car and exploring. Maybe Hallasan.
Road trip style — and I want to do Hallasan.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Hallasan is beautiful. Make sure you check the trail conditions.
dialogue.ko: 한라산 진짜 예뻐. 등산로 상태 꼭 확인해봐.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Good tip. Any restaurants you'd recommend?
dialogue.ko: 좋은 팁이다. 추천 식당 있어?
alt_en: Oh, I'll check. Know any good spots to eat?
Got it. Anything you'd say I have to try?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You have to try the black pork. There's a street near Dongmun market.
dialogue.ko: 흑돼지는 꼭 먹어야 해. 동문시장 근처 골목 있어.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'll add that to the list. Thanks for the tips.
dialogue.ko: 리스트에 추가해야겠다. 팁 고마워.
alt_en: Noted. I'll look it up.
Perfect. Adding it now.

key_expressions.en: How long are you going for?
key_expressions.note: 여행 기간 묻기. 'How many days?' 보다 자연스럽다
등산 전 사전 조사 권고 표현

key_expressions.en: I'll add that to the list
key_expressions.note: 추천받은 것을 기억하겠다는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I'm going for 5 days vacation' → 'I'm going for five days' (vacation 불필요)
'Any restaurant recommendation?' → 'Any restaurants you'd recommend?' (복수형 + 동사 패턴 주의)
'I never went' → 'I've never been' (경험 표현에는 현재완료 사용)

scenarios.context_ko: 연속 야근으로 지친 상태, 동료에게 토로하기

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You look tired. Long night?
dialogue.ko: 너 피곤해 보여. 어젯밤도 늦었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. Third night in a row. I didn't leave until like ten.
dialogue.ko: 응. 3일 연속이야. 어제도 10시는 넘어서 나왔어.
alt_en: Third late night running. Left around ten again.
Yep — three days straight. Got out past ten.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Three nights in a row — that's rough. Is it the Seo account?
dialogue.ko: 3일 연속이면 힘들겠다. 서 대리 건이야?
dialogue.recast_note: 'Third night in a row' → 'Three nights in a row' + 강조로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. The deadline keeps moving, and nobody's helping out.
dialogue.ko: 응. 마감은 계속 바뀌고, 아무도 도와주질 않아.
alt_en: The Seo stuff keeps expanding and I'm handling it solo.
Yeah — shifting deadline, no backup.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's not sustainable. Have you talked to anyone about it?
dialogue.ko: 그건 장기적으로 못 버텨. 누구한테 말해봤어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Not yet. I don't want to, you know, seem like I'm complaining.
dialogue.ko: 아직. 뭔가, 있잖아, 불평하는 것처럼 보이기 싫어서.
alt_en: No — I don't want it to come across as whining.
Not yet. I'm worried it'll sound like I'm making excuses.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It's not complaining. It's a workload issue. Just frame it that way.
dialogue.ko: 불평이 아니야. 업무량 문제야. 그렇게 말하면 돼.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I mean, you're right. Maybe I'll bring it up tomorrow.
dialogue.ko: 뭐, 맞는 말이야. 내일 한번 꺼내볼게.
alt_en: Fair point. I'll mention it in tomorrow's check-in.
Yeah, you're right. I'll bring it up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Do it. You've got to push back sometimes.
dialogue.ko: 해. 때로는 말해야 해.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. Thanks for the reality check.
dialogue.ko: 그래. 현실적인 조언 고마워.
alt_en: Appreciate it. I needed that.
Thanks. Good to hear it from someone else.

key_expressions.note: 연속 기간 표현. in a row = 연속으로
지속 불가능한 상황 표현
같은 내용을 다른 각도로 표현할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'Three nights continuously' → 'three nights in a row' ('continuously'는 문어체, 구어체는 'in a row')
'I will bring it out' → 'I'll bring it up' (화제를 꺼낼 때는 bring up)
'Push back'을 '뒤로 미루다'로 오해 — 여기서는 '반박하다, 저항하다'의 의미

scenarios.context_ko: Excel 작업 막힌 부분을 동료에게 도움 요청하기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, do you have a second? I'm stuck on something.
dialogue.ko: 저기, 잠깐 시간 돼? 막히는 게 있어서.
alt_en: Mind helping me with something real quick?
Got a minute? I need a hand with something.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Sure, what's up?
dialogue.ko: 그래, 무슨 일이야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I'm trying to do a VLOOKUP and the formula keeps, um, giving me an error.
dialogue.ko: VLOOKUP 하려는데 수식이 계속, 음, 오류가 나.
alt_en: My VLOOKUP formula keeps breaking.
I can't get this VLOOKUP to work — keeps erroring out.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: VLOOKUP throwing errors? Usually it's the range or the match column. Can I see?
dialogue.ko: VLOOKUP 오류? 보통 범위나 기준 열 문제야. 봐도 돼?
dialogue.recast_note: 'gives me an error' → 'throwing errors'로 더 자연스러운 표현으로 paraphrase

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, please. I've been looking at this for like twenty minutes.
dialogue.ko: 응, 와줘. 20분 동안 보고 있었어.
alt_en: Please. I've been staring at this forever.
Yeah — been stuck on it for a while.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ah — your lookup column isn't sorted. That's why it's breaking.
dialogue.ko: 아 — 기준 열이 정렬이 안 돼 있네. 그래서 오류 나는 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh wow, that's it? I would never have figured that out.
dialogue.ko: 오, 진짜? 그거였어? 절대 못 찾았을 것 같은데.
alt_en: No way — that's all it was?
I'd have been at this all day. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Easy fix. Add a sort and you're good.
dialogue.ko: 쉽게 고쳐. 정렬 추가하면 돼.

key_expressions.note: 도움 요청 전 사전 확인. 'Do you have time?' 보다 부드럽다
진행이 막혔을 때 표준 표현

key_expressions.en: I would never have figured that out
key_expressions.note: 가정법 과거완료. 도움에 감사할 때

common_mistakes_ko: 'Can you help me for a second?' → 'Do you have a second?' (시간을 먼저 확인하는 게 더 자연스러운 순서)
'I cannot find it' → 'I'm stuck on it' (문제가 막혔다는 표현)
'VLOOKUP makes error' → 'VLOOKUP is throwing an error' / 'keeps giving me an error'

scenarios.context_ko: 하루 일 끝내고 동료들에게 퇴근 인사 나누기

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Alright, I'm heading out. See everyone tomorrow.
dialogue.ko: 자, 나 간다. 내일 봐.
alt_en: Okay, I'm out. Later everyone.
Taking off — see you all tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Already? Nice — have a good one!
dialogue.ko: 벌써? 좋겠다 — 좋은 저녁!

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You too. Don't stay too late.
dialogue.ko: 너도. 너무 늦게까지 있지 마.
alt_en: Same to you. Get out of here at a reasonable hour.
You too — don't overdo it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha, no promises. See you tomorrow.
dialogue.ko: 하, 장담은 못 하지. 내일 봐.
dialogue.recast_note: 'Don't stay too late' → 'no promises'로 유머 있게 반응하며 의미를 받아침

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Take care, everyone.
dialogue.ko: 모두 잘 가.
alt_en: Good night, everyone.
Night! Take care.

key_expressions.note: 퇴근·자리 떠날 때 표준 표현. 'I'm leaving' 보다 더 자연스럽다
시간대 무관하게 쓸 수 있는 인사
확답 피할 때 유머 있는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I'm going home' → 'I'm heading out' (미국 직장 구어체에서 더 자연스러운 퇴근 표현)
'You too good night' → 'You too. Have a good one.' (단순히 'You too'만으로 충분)
'Don't be late' → 'Don't stay too late' (늦게까지 있지 말라는 표현)

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 카페에서 최근 여행 이야기를 나눈다

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh wow, you're back! How was the trip? I've been dying to hear.
dialogue.ko: 야, 돌아왔구나! 여행 어땠어? 얘기 너무 듣고 싶었다.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: It was amazing. Um, the landscape there was — I don't know how to say — like very different from here.
dialogue.ko: 진짜 대단했어. 음, 거기 풍경이 — 어떻게 말하지 — 여기랑 완전 달랐어.
alt_en: It was incredible. The scenery was just totally unlike anything I've seen here.
Honestly, I was blown away. The landscape was nothing like what we have here.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Yeah, the scenery there is supposed to be breathtaking. What part stood out the most?
dialogue.ko: 맞아, 거기 경치 장난 아니라고 들었어. 어느 부분이 제일 기억에 남아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The mountains, definitely. We hiked for like three hours and then — boom — the view just opened up. I couldn't believe it.
dialogue.ko: 산이 최고였어. 세 시간 정도 올라갔더니 — 짠 — 갑자기 뷰가 탁 트이는 거야. 믿기지가 않았어.
alt_en: Definitely the mountains. We hiked three hours and suddenly the whole view just opened up in front of us.
The mountain views, for sure. After three hours of hiking, the panorama just hit you all at once.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That sounds like a real payoff moment — worth every step of the climb.
dialogue.ko: 그야말로 고생 끝에 낙이 온 순간이네 — 올라간 보람이 있었겠다.
dialogue.recast_note: 학습자의 'the view just opened up'을 'real payoff moment'로 recast — 극적 순간을 보상 개념으로 자연스럽게 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Totally. And, uh, the food was another thing. Every meal was like — I can't explain — just so fresh.
dialogue.ko: 완전. 그리고, 어, 음식도 대박이었어. 매 끼니가 — 설명을 못 하겠는데 — 그냥 너무 신선했어.
alt_en: Exactly. And the food was on another level — everything tasted so fresh, I can't even describe it.
For real. Plus the food was incredible. Every single meal was just so fresh, I don't know how to put it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Fresh as in local ingredients, or was the cooking style different?
dialogue.ko: 신선하다는 게 재료가 현지산이라는 건지, 아니면 조리 방식이 달랐던 건지?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Both, I think. Like everything was from the market that morning. You could just taste the difference.
dialogue.ko: 둘 다인 것 같아. 아침 시장에서 바로 사 온 것들이잖아. 맛이 다른 게 느껴지더라고.
alt_en: Both, honestly. Everything was from the morning market — you could really taste how fresh it was.
I think both. They'd buy straight from the market that day, and the difference was obvious.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That makes such a difference. Okay, would you go back?
dialogue.ko: 그게 진짜 차이를 만들지. 그래서, 다시 가고 싶어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Without question. I'm already looking at flights for next year.
dialogue.ko: 당연하죠. 이미 내년 항공편 알아보고 있어.
alt_en: A hundred percent. I've already started looking at flights for next year.
Absolutely, no doubt. I'm already checking flights for next year.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Count me in next time.
dialogue.ko: 다음에는 나도 껴줘.

key_expressions.note: 경치가 갑자기 눈앞에 펼쳐지는 극적 순간 묘사
노력·기다림의 보상이 온 순간
참여 의사를 캐주얼하게 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'the scenery was very different' 대신 한국식 직역 'the scenery was very difference'처럼 명사/형용사 혼용 오류
'I can't believe' 대신 'I can't believe it'처럼 목적어 생략 없이 쓰는 것이 자연스러움 — 'I couldn't believe' 시제 일치도 주의
'Count me in' 대신 'Include me next time'처럼 격식체로 쓰는 실수 — 친구 대화에서는 'Count me in'이 훨씬 자연스러움
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국인 친구에게 여행 경험을 나눌 때 구체적인 '감각 묘사'(smell, taste, view)를 넣으면 대화가 훨씬 살아난다. 한국식으로 '좋았어'로 끝내면 대화가 닫히는 느낌을 준다.

scenarios.context_ko: 후배 동료에게 첫 직장 경험담을 솔직하게 나눈다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, um, can I ask — what was your first job like? I'm kind of nervous about starting next week.
dialogue.ko: 저기, 음, 여쭤봐도 될까요 — 첫 직장이 어땠어요? 다음 주 시작하는 게 좀 긴장돼서요.
alt_en: Uh, mind if I ask — what was your first job actually like? I start next week and I'm a little nervous.
Hey, can I pick your brain? What was your first job like? I'm kind of anxious about starting next week.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, of course. Honestly? I was a mess the first month. Everyone is.
dialogue.ko: 물론이죠. 솔직히? 첫 달은 완전히 엉망이었어요. 다들 그래요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Really? I kind of thought people who already work there — like they know everything already.
dialogue.ko: 진짜요? 이미 일하는 분들은 다 알고 계시는 줄 알았어요.
alt_en: Seriously? I assumed the people already there would know all the ropes.
No way. I figured the people working there already had everything figured out.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Not at all. The biggest thing I learned was that it's okay to ask questions. Like, asking is way better than guessing and getting it wrong.
dialogue.ko: 전혀요. 제가 배운 가장 중요한 건 질문해도 된다는 거였어요. 추측하다가 틀리는 것보다 묻는 게 훨씬 낫거든요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I worry that people will think I'm, you know, not smart if I ask too many things.
dialogue.ko: 질문을 너무 많이 하면 사람들이 저를, 있잖아요, 똑똑하지 않다고 생각할까 봐 걱정돼요.
alt_en: I'm worried people will think I'm not capable if I keep asking questions.
I'm scared that asking a lot will make me look like I don't know what I'm doing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's actually the opposite of how most managers see it. They'd rather you speak up than stay silent and make a costly mistake.
dialogue.ko: 실제로는 대부분의 관리자들이 정반대로 생각해요. 조용히 있다가 큰 실수를 저지르는 것보다 적극적으로 말하는 걸 훨씬 선호하거든요.
dialogue.recast_note: 'people will think I'm not smart'를 'speak up'으로 recast — 소극적 우려를 능동적 행동 언어로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That makes sense. Was there a moment, like, when you really felt comfortable?
dialogue.ko: 그 말이 맞네요. 진짜로, 편안해진다고 느꼈던 순간이 있었나요?
alt_en: That makes sense. Was there a specific moment when things started to click?
I get that. Was there a turning point when you actually started feeling comfortable?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: About three months in. I finished a project on my own and my manager said it was solid. That changed everything.
dialogue.ko: 한 세 달쯤 됐을 때요. 혼자 프로젝트를 마쳤는데 팀장님이 잘 했다고 하시더라고요. 그게 다 바꿔놨어요.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Three months — okay, I can wait that long. I'll try to keep that in mind.
dialogue.ko: 세 달이면 — 그 정도는 버틸 수 있겠어요. 그 말 기억해 둘게요.
alt_en: Three months — that's manageable. I'll keep that in mind.
Okay, three months is doable. I'll try to hold on to that.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You'll get there. And honestly, the jitters you feel right now? That means you care.
dialogue.ko: 잘 될 거예요. 솔직히, 지금 긴장되는 거? 그건 신경 쓴다는 증거예요.

key_expressions.ko: 모든 걸 이미 알다 / 요령을 다 알다
key_expressions.note: 직장·환경에 완전히 익숙한 상태를 뜻하는 관용표현
침묵하지 않고 자기 생각이나 질문을 내놓는 행위
시작 전 느끼는 초조하고 떨리는 감각을 가리키는 구어 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'I'm nervous' 대신 'I'm nervous about to' 형태로 'to부정사' 잘못 연결 — 'nervous about + -ing/명사'가 맞는 구조
'make a mistake' 대신 'do a mistake'로 쓰는 오류 — make를 써야 한다
'speak up'의 발음·억양을 'speak' 단독으로 끊는 경우 — 'up'까지 함께 붙여 올려 말해야 자연스럽다
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 미국 직장 문화에서는 신입이 '모르면 물어보라'는 분위기가 강한 편. 침묵보다 질문이 능동적·긍정적 태도로 해석되는 경우가 많다.

scenarios.context_ko: 친한 친구와 산책 중 힘들었던 과거를 이야기한다

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You've seemed quieter lately. Everything okay?
dialogue.ko: 요즘 좀 조용해 보이더라. 다 괜찮아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, I'm fine. I was just thinking about, uh, a really hard time I had a few years ago.
dialogue.ko: 응, 괜찮아. 그냥 몇 년 전에 진짜 힘들었던 때를 생각하고 있었어.
alt_en: I'm good. I was just reflecting on a really tough period I went through a few years back.
Yeah, fine. I was just remembering this really difficult stretch I had a couple years ago.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Want to talk about it? No pressure.
dialogue.ko: 얘기하고 싶어? 부담 없이.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sure. Um, I lost my job and then my apartment — everything kind of fell apart at the same time.
dialogue.ko: 그럴게. 음, 직장을 잃고 나서 아파트도 — 동시에 다 무너지는 것 같았어.
alt_en: Okay. I lost my job and then my place — it all kind of came apart at once.
Yeah. I got laid off, then lost my apartment — everything collapsed at the same time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's a lot to go through at once. How long did it take to get back on your feet?
dialogue.ko: 한꺼번에 겪기엔 너무 많은 거잖아. 다시 일어서는 데 얼마나 걸렸어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'everything fell apart'를 'get back on your feet'으로 recast — 붕괴 이미지를 회복 지향적 표현으로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Like eight or nine months? I stayed at my brother's place. I kind of had to start over completely.
dialogue.ko: 한 여덟, 아홉 달? 동생네 집에 있었어. 완전 처음부터 다시 시작해야 했지.
alt_en: About eight or nine months. I crashed at my brother's and had to basically start from scratch.
Eight or nine months, maybe. I stayed with my brother and had to rebuild everything from the ground up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's rough. What kept you going?
dialogue.ko: 힘들었겠다. 뭐가 버티게 해줬어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Honestly, my brother. And, well, just knowing that it couldn't stay like that forever.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히, 동생이요. 그리고, 뭐, 이 상태가 영원히 지속될 수는 없다는 걸 알았던 것도.
alt_en: Honestly? My brother. And just believing that things couldn't stay that way forever.
My brother, mostly. And knowing deep down it had to get better at some point.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You came out of it stronger, though. That's clear.
dialogue.ko: 근데 그거 겪고 더 단단해진 거 티 나. 그건 분명해.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I guess so. It changed how I look at things for sure.
dialogue.ko: 그런가. 그 일이 세상 보는 방식을 확실히 바꿔놓긴 했어.
alt_en: Maybe. It definitely shifted how I see things.
I think so. It really changed my perspective on a lot of things.

key_expressions.note: 여러 일이 동시에 안 풀리거나 상황이 붕괴될 때 쓰는 표현
어려움 후 자립·회복하는 과정을 뜻하는 관용구
힘든 상황에서 동기·지지를 물을 때 자연스러운 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'fall apart'를 'fall down'으로 대체하는 실수 — fall down은 물리적으로 넘어지는 것, fall apart는 상황·관계가 무너지는 것
'get back on my feet'에서 'on my foot'처럼 단수 쓰는 오류 — 관용구는 항상 복수 feet
'What kept you going?'을 'What made you keep going?'으로 길게 쓰는 한국인 습관 — 짧게 'What kept you going?'이 더 자연스럽다

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 대화 중 인생 가장 행복한 기억을 꺼낸다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Can I tell you something kind of random? I was thinking about the happiest moment of my life.
dialogue.ko: 좀 뜬금없는 얘기 해도 돼? 내 인생에서 가장 행복했던 순간을 생각하고 있었어.
alt_en: Random thought, but — I've been thinking about the happiest moment of my life.
This is out of nowhere, but I keep thinking about what the best moment of my life was.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh, I love this. What is it?
dialogue.ko: 오, 좋은데. 뭔데?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The day my son was born. Like, nothing else comes close.
dialogue.ko: 아들이 태어난 날. 다른 어떤 것도 비교가 안 돼.
alt_en: The day my son was born. Nothing else even compares.
When my son was born. Honestly, everything else pales in comparison.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's beautiful. Do you remember the exact moment he was handed to you?
dialogue.ko: 너무 좋다. 처음 안겨준 그 순간 기억해?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Every detail. He was so small. I just, uh, didn't know what to do with my hands.
dialogue.ko: 모든 순간. 정말 작았어. 그냥, 어, 손을 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어.
alt_en: Every single detail. He was tiny. I didn't even know what to do with my hands.
Every detail, yes. He was so small — I had no idea how to hold him.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha, I can picture that. You were probably completely overwhelmed in the best possible way.
dialogue.ko: 하, 상상이 가. 완전히 압도됐겠다, 가장 좋은 의미에서.
dialogue.recast_note: 'didn't know what to do with my hands'를 'completely overwhelmed in the best possible way'로 recast — 어색함·당황을 감동적 압도감으로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly that. I actually cried, which I never do. My wife still teases me about it.
dialogue.ko: 딱 그거야. 실제로 울었어, 나 원래 안 우는데. 아직도 아내가 놀려.
alt_en: That's exactly it. I cried — which almost never happens. My wife still brings it up.
Perfectly said. I even cried, which is very unlike me. My wife never lets me forget it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's such a sweet memory. Has anything come close since?
dialogue.ko: 너무 좋은 기억이다. 그 이후로 비슷하게 행복한 순간이 있었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: There are a lot of good moments. But that one — I think that one stays first.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 순간들이 많지. 근데 그 순간은 — 계속 첫 번째인 것 같아.
alt_en: There've been so many great moments. But that one will probably always be number one.
Plenty of good ones. But that day? I think it'll always hold the top spot.

key_expressions.ko: 다른 어떤 것도 비교가 안 된다
key_expressions.note: 비교 불가한 최고임을 강조하는 표현

key_expressions.en: overwhelmed in the best possible way
key_expressions.note: 감동으로 벅찬 상태를 표현할 때 쓰는 구

key_expressions.ko: 절대 잊게 내버려두지 않는다 / 계속 들먹인다
key_expressions.note: 누군가가 특정 사건을 계속 언급·놀려댈 때 쓰는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'Nothing comes close'에서 'close'를 'closer'로 비교급 쓰는 오류 — 부정문+come close는 원급으로 씀
'teases me about it'을 'makes fun of me'로만 알고 tease를 못 쓰는 경우 — tease가 더 친근하고 자연스러운 표현
'I actually cried' 대신 'I was crying'으로 과거진행으로 쓰는 실수 — 단발 완료 행위에는 단순과거 did가 더 자연스럽다

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 함께 웃으며 민망했던 과거 일화를 공유한다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey — okay, I'm going to tell you something embarrassing. Promise you won't laugh.
dialogue.ko: 야 — 있잖아, 민망한 거 하나 얘기할게. 웃지 않겠다고 약속해.
alt_en: Okay, I have to tell you something super embarrassing. You have to promise not to laugh.
Hey, I'm going to share something embarrassing. Swear you won't laugh.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No promises. Go ahead.
dialogue.ko: 약속은 못 하겠는데. 어서 해봐.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: So I showed up to a work presentation in, um, completely different shoes — like one black, one brown.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까, 회사 발표에 음, 신발을 완전히 다르게 신고 갔어 — 한 짝은 검정, 한 짝은 갈색.
alt_en: I walked into a work presentation wearing two completely different shoes — one black, one brown.
I turned up to this big work presentation with one black shoe and one brown shoe on.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: No way! Did anyone notice?
dialogue.ko: 설마! 누가 눈치챘어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: My manager. Right at the start. He looked down, and I just — I wanted to disappear.
dialogue.ko: 팀장님이. 딱 시작하자마자. 아래를 쳐다보는데, 나는 그냥 — 사라지고 싶었어.
alt_en: My manager noticed, right at the beginning. He glanced down and I just wanted to vanish.
My manager caught it immediately. He looked at my feet and I just wanted to sink into the floor.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha! Did he say anything, or did he just let you suffer through it?
dialogue.ko: 하하! 뭐라고 하던가요, 아니면 그냥 고통받게 내버려뒀어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'I wanted to disappear'를 'let you suffer through it'으로 recast — 사라지고 싶은 수치심을 견뎌내는 고통으로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: He just smiled. Didn't say a word. Which was somehow worse.
dialogue.ko: 그냥 웃기만 했어. 아무 말도 안 했어. 어떻게 그게 더 나빴어.
alt_en: He just smiled. Said nothing. Which honestly made it worse somehow.
He smiled and stayed silent. Which, for some reason, felt even more embarrassing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That silence is brutal. At least if he'd laughed, it'd be over faster.
dialogue.ko: 그 침묵은 진짜 잔인하지. 차라리 웃었으면 빨리 끝났을 텐데.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. I checked my feet every morning for like a month after that.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그 후로 한 달은 매일 아침 발을 확인했어.
alt_en: Right. For a month after that, I double-checked my shoes every single morning.
Yes. I inspected my shoes every morning for a solid month after that.

key_expressions.note: 극도의 창피함을 느낄 때 쓰는 구어 표현
믿기 어려운 상황에 쓰는 감탄사
불편하거나 창피한 상황을 끝까지 감내하는 것을 뜻함

common_mistakes_ko: 'I wanted to disappear'를 'I wanted to vanish myself'처럼 재귀 목적어 잘못 붙이는 오류 — 'disappear'는 목적어 불필요
'somehow worse'에서 somehow 위치를 문장 맨 앞에 놓는 실수 — 'somehow'가 형용사 앞에 와야 뉘앙스가 살아남
'No way!' 대신 'Impossible!'로 직역하는 경우 — No way가 훨씬 자연스러운 구어 반응

scenarios.context_ko: 외국 친구와 처음 해외에서 겪은 당황스러웠던 순간을 나눈다

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You mentioned you'd been abroad before — where was the most different place you visited?
dialogue.ko: 예전에 해외 다녀온 적 있다고 했잖아 — 가장 달랐던 곳이 어디야?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Um, probably India. I was not prepared at all. Like, everything was — I don't know — just so much.
dialogue.ko: 음, 아마 인도? 전혀 준비가 안 돼 있었어. 그냥, 모든 게 — 어떻게 말하지 — 너무 많았어.
alt_en: Probably India. I had no idea what to expect. Everything was just so overwhelming.
India, for sure. I was completely unprepared. Everything hit me at once — sights, sounds, everything.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: India can be intense! What hit you first?
dialogue.ko: 인도는 강렬하지! 뭐가 제일 먼저 충격이었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The traffic. There were no — like — lanes. Everyone just, uh, went wherever they wanted. And horns everywhere.
dialogue.ko: 교통. 차선이 — 그냥 — 없었어. 다들 그냥, 어, 가고 싶은 데로 갔어. 그리고 클락션 소리가 사방에서.
alt_en: The traffic. There were basically no lanes — everyone just drove wherever they felt like. And the constant honking.
Traffic, definitely. No lanes, no rules — everyone just went wherever. And horns nonstop.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's the classic India initiation. Did you ever get used to it?
dialogue.ko: 그게 전형적인 인도 적응 과정이지. 결국 익숙해졌어?
dialogue.recast_note: 'horns everywhere' 충격을 'classic India initiation'으로 recast — 충격 경험을 통과의례 언어로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: After like five days, yeah. I actually started tuning it out. But the first day I just stood on the sidewalk — frozen.
dialogue.ko: 한 5일 지나니까, 응. 오히려 그냥 배경 소리처럼 됐어. 근데 첫날엔 그냥 인도에 서서 — 굳어버렸어.
alt_en: After five days or so, yes. I started blocking it out. But day one I just froze on the sidewalk.
About five days in, I got used to it. I could tune it out. First day though — I just stood there, completely frozen.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Five days is actually pretty fast. Did any food moments surprise you?
dialogue.ko: 5일이면 사실 꽤 빠른 적응이야. 음식에서 놀랐던 순간도 있었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Oh yes. I ordered what I thought was mild curry, and — well — my face turned completely red.
dialogue.ko: 아, 맞아. 순한 카레라고 생각하고 시켰는데 — 뭐 — 얼굴이 완전 빨개졌어.
alt_en: Oh definitely. I ordered something I thought was mild curry and — yeah — my face went bright red.
Yes. I ordered what I thought was a mild dish. Let's just say my face told a different story.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ha! Did the locals think that was hilarious?
dialogue.ko: 하! 현지인들이 엄청 웃었겠다?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: The waiter was very polite, but yes, people at the next table were definitely holding back laughs.
dialogue.ko: 웨이터는 매우 정중했는데, 옆 테이블 사람들은 확실히 웃음 참고 있었어.
alt_en: The waiter was polite about it, but the table next to us was definitely suppressing laughs.
The waiter kept it professional, but the people at the next table were definitely trying not to laugh.

key_expressions.note: 낯선 환경에 처음 노출되는 경험을 의식처럼 표현
소음이나 자극에 더 이상 반응하지 않게 되는 것
'suppressing laughter'보다 구어적으로 자주 쓰이는 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'tune it out'을 모르고 'ignore it'으로만 대체하는 경우 — tune out은 의식적으로 주의를 끊는 뉘앙스로 더 정확
'my face turned red' 대신 'my face became red'처럼 become 동사를 쓰는 오류 — turn이 색·상태 변화에 더 자연스럽다
'hold back laughs'를 'hold my laughter'처럼 단수 laughter로 표현하는 경우 — hold back laughs가 구어에서 더 자연스럽다
scenarios.cultural_note_ko: 인도에서 '순한 맛(mild)'은 한국의 기준과 다를 수 있다. 현지인 기준의 mild도 한국인 입맛에는 상당히 매울 수 있으므로 메뉴 주문 시 'very mild' 또는 'no spice please'가 더 안전하다.

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 이야기 중 자신에게 큰 영향을 준 사람을 떠올린다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey, um, random — was there anyone in your life who really shaped who you are?
dialogue.ko: 있잖아, 음, 갑자기 생각났는데 — 네가 지금 이렇게 된 데 정말 영향을 준 사람이 있어?
alt_en: Hey, out of nowhere — was there someone who really shaped who you became?
Random question — was there a person who had a big influence on who you are today?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: My high school coach, without question. Why — who's on your mind?
dialogue.ko: 고등학교 때 코치님, 당연히. 왜 — 누구 생각하고 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: My first boss. She was — I mean — very demanding. But she believed in me before I believed in myself.
dialogue.ko: 첫 번째 상사. 그분이 — 있잖아 — 정말 요구하는 게 많았어. 근데 내가 나를 믿기 전부터 나를 믿어줬어.
alt_en: My first boss. She was incredibly demanding, but she believed in me before I even believed in myself.
My first manager. Really tough — but she had more faith in me than I had in myself at the time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's the best kind. The ones who push you because they see what you can't see yet.
dialogue.ko: 그게 최고의 사람이지. 네가 아직 못 보는 걸 보고 밀어붙이는 사람.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. She used to say — um — 'comfort is the enemy of growth.' I didn't understand it at the time.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그분이 자주 말씀하셨어 — 음 — '편안함이 성장의 적이다.' 그때는 이해를 못 했어.
alt_en: Exactly. She always said, 'Comfort is the enemy of growth.' I didn't get it back then.
Totally. She had this line — 'Comfort is the enemy of growth.' I couldn't understand it at the time.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: And now it makes complete sense. You had to live through it to get what she meant.
dialogue.ko: 그리고 이제는 완전히 이해되는 거지. 직접 살아봐야 그 말이 뭔 뜻인지 알게 되는 거야.
dialogue.recast_note: 'I didn't understand it at the time'을 'you had to live through it to get what she meant'으로 recast — 이해 못 함을 경험을 통한 이해로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's it. She also gave me my first real responsibility and — well — I almost blew it.
dialogue.ko: 바로 그거야. 그분이 처음으로 진짜 책임을 맡겨주셨는데 — 뭐 — 거의 망칠 뻔했어.
alt_en: Exactly. She gave me my first real responsibility and I nearly messed it up.
Right. She handed me my first real task — and I almost completely screwed it up.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: But you didn't. And I bet she knew you'd pull through.
dialogue.ko: 근데 안 그랬잖아. 네가 해낼 거 그분은 알았을 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. I've tried to do the same for people who work with me.
dialogue.ko: 응. 나도 나랑 같이 일하는 사람들한테 그렇게 해주려고 해.
alt_en: Yeah. I try to pass that on to the people I work with now.
I do. I've tried to pay it forward with the people on my team.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's the cycle. Good mentors create more mentors.
dialogue.ko: 그게 연결되는 거지. 좋은 멘토가 더 많은 멘토를 만들어내는 거야.

key_expressions.en: believed in me before I believed in myself
key_expressions.ko: 내가 스스로를 믿기 전에 나를 믿어주다
key_expressions.note: 멘토·지지자를 설명할 때 자주 쓰이는 감동적 표현
실수나 실패 직전까지 갔음을 표현하는 구어
자신이 받은 도움을 다음 사람에게 전달하는 행위

common_mistakes_ko: 'she believed in me' 뒤에 'than myself'를 붙여 비교구조를 만들려는 실수 — 'before I believed in myself'처럼 시간 부사절이 더 자연스럽다
'almost blew it'을 'almost failed it'으로 대체하는 경우 — blow it은 기회·임무를 망치는 것으로 구어 특유의 뉘앙스가 있다
'pay it forward'의 의미를 모르고 'give it back'으로 쓰는 오류 — pay back은 빚 상환, pay forward는 선순환 전달

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 인생을 바꾼 결정에 대해 솔직하게 이야기한다

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: You seem like a totally different person than you were two years ago. Something changed, didn't it?
dialogue.ko: 2년 전이랑 완전히 다른 사람 같아. 뭔가 바뀐 거지?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, a lot changed. I quit my job and moved to a different city. It was — uh — kind of a leap.
dialogue.ko: 응, 많이 바뀌었어. 직장 그만두고 다른 도시로 이사했어. 그게 — 어 — 좀 큰 도전이었어.
alt_en: Yeah, a lot. I left my job and moved to a new city. It was kind of a big leap.
A lot. I quit my job and relocated. It was, honestly, a pretty significant leap of faith.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Both at the same time? That's brave. What pushed you over the edge?
dialogue.ko: 동시에 둘 다? 용감하다. 뭐가 결정적이었어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I woke up one morning and just — I couldn't make myself go to work. I realized I had been running on empty for years.
dialogue.ko: 어느 날 아침에 일어났는데 그냥 — 출근하고 싶은 마음이 없었어. 몇 년간 완전히 바닥난 상태로 달려왔다는 걸 깨달았어.
alt_en: One morning I woke up and couldn't bring myself to go in. I realized I'd been running on empty for years.
I woke up one day and just couldn't do it. I finally realized I'd been burning out for years without admitting it.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That kind of burnout creeps up on you slowly, and then it just hits all at once.
dialogue.ko: 그런 번아웃은 서서히 다가오다가, 어느 순간 한꺼번에 터지는 거지.
dialogue.recast_note: 'running on empty'를 'burnout'으로 명시하고 'creeps up / hits all at once'로 recast — 학습자의 은유를 구체적인 심리 개념으로 자연스럽게 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. And the move — well — I had always wanted to live in a smaller city. Less pressure.
dialogue.ko: 딱 맞아. 그리고 이사는 — 뭐 — 항상 더 작은 도시에서 살고 싶었어. 덜 압박감이 있는.
alt_en: Exactly. And I'd always wanted to try living in a smaller city — somewhere with less pressure.
That's it. And the move was something I'd always wanted — a smaller city, less stress.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Do you feel like you made the right call?
dialogue.ko: 잘한 결정이었다고 느껴?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: A hundred percent. Scary at first, but — I mean — I sleep better, I think more clearly.
dialogue.ko: 백퍼센트. 처음엔 무서웠는데, 근데 — 있잖아 — 이제 더 잘 자고, 더 명확하게 생각하게 됐어.
alt_en: Completely. It was scary at first, but I sleep better now and think more clearly.
Without question. Terrifying at first — but now I sleep well and my head is clear.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That says it all. Some risks are worth taking.
dialogue.ko: 그 말이 다 설명해주네. 어떤 위험은 감수할 만한 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I wish I'd done it sooner, honestly.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히, 더 일찍 했더라면 좋았을 것 같아.
alt_en: Honestly, I just wish I hadn't waited so long.
My only regret is that I didn't make the move sooner.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: But you got there. That's what counts.
dialogue.ko: 근데 결국 했잖아. 그게 중요한 거야.

key_expressions.note: 연료 없이 달리는 차 비유 — 에너지·여력이 완전히 소진된 상태
최종 결정을 내리게 만든 마지막 요인을 물을 때 쓰는 표현
결정·선택이 옳았는지 되돌아볼 때 쓰는 구어 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'running on empty'를 직역해 'running without energy'로 쓰는 경우 — 관용표현 그대로 익혀야 자연스럽다
'pushed over the edge'를 부정적 의미(폭발·분노)로만 아는 경우 — 긍정적 결단의 계기로도 쓸 수 있다
'a hundred percent' 대신 'one hundred percent'처럼 완전히 쓰는 경우 — 구어에서는 'a hundred percent'가 더 자연스럽다

scenarios.context_ko: 친한 친구와 가족 갈등 이후 화해 과정을 솔직하게 나눈다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I finally talked to my sister. After, like, three months of not speaking.
dialogue.ko: 드디어 동생이랑 이야기했어. 대략 세 달간 말 안 하다가.
alt_en: I finally reached out to my sister — after about three months of silence.
I finally talked things out with my sister. Three months of not speaking.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Oh wow. How did it go?
dialogue.ko: 아 진짜. 어떻게 됐어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Better than I expected. Um, I was the one who reached out first. It was hard to do.
dialogue.ko: 생각보다 잘 됐어. 음, 내가 먼저 연락했어. 하기가 쉽지 않았어.
alt_en: Better than I thought. I was the one who made the first move. That wasn't easy.
Way better than expected. I reached out first — which was hard.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That takes guts. Usually whoever goes first breaks the ice for both people.
dialogue.ko: 용기 있는 거야. 보통 먼저 나서는 쪽이 두 사람 다를 위해 분위기를 먼저 깨는 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah. I — I mean — I said what I felt. That I was sorry for my part. Not everything, but my part.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 나는 — 있잖아 — 내가 느낀 걸 말했어. 내가 잘못한 부분에 대해 미안하다고. 전부가 아니라, 내 부분만.
alt_en: I said what I felt. I apologized for my part — not everything, just what I actually did wrong.
I just said it straight — I was sorry for my part in it. Not all of it, but what I did.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's the right way to do it — owning your side without taking blame for the whole thing.
dialogue.ko: 그게 맞는 방식이야 — 전부 다 뒤집어쓰지 않고 네 부분만 인정하는 거.
dialogue.recast_note: 'sorry for my part'를 'owning your side without taking blame for the whole thing'으로 recast — 부분적 책임 인정을 더 명확한 개념으로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. And she — well — she came around too. Not instantly, but by the end we were actually laughing.
dialogue.ko: 딱 그거야. 그리고 동생도 — 뭐 — 마음이 풀렸어. 바로는 아니었는데, 결국엔 진짜 같이 웃고 있었어.
alt_en: Exactly. And she came around too — not right away, but by the end we were laughing together.
That's it. And she softened too. Not immediately, but by the time we wrapped up, we were actually laughing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Laughing — that's when you know you're actually okay.
dialogue.ko: 웃었다 — 그때가 진짜 괜찮아진 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I know. I feel so much lighter now. I didn't realize how heavy it was weighing on me.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 지금 훨씬 홀가분해. 그게 얼마나 무겁게 짓눌리고 있었는지 몰랐어.
alt_en: I know. I feel so much lighter now — I didn't realize how much it was weighing on me.
Right. It's like a weight off. I didn't know how much it was dragging me down.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Three months is a long time to carry that. You should be proud of yourself for making that call.
dialogue.ko: 세 달이나 그걸 안고 산 거잖아. 먼저 연락한 거 스스로 자랑스러워해도 돼.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Thanks. I just wish it hadn't taken this long.
dialogue.ko: 고마워. 그냥 이렇게 오래 걸리지 않았으면 좋았을 텐데.
alt_en: Thanks. I just wish we hadn't waited so long.
Thanks. I just wish it hadn't taken three months to get here.

key_expressions.note: 갈등이나 어색함이 있는 관계에서 먼저 대화를 시작하는 것
전부 다 책임지는 것이 아닌 본인 부분만 솔직히 인정하는 행위
갈등·걱정이 해소된 후 심리적 무게가 줄어든 느낌

common_mistakes_ko: 'break the ice'를 'break the atmosphere'로 직역하는 오류 — break the ice가 고정 관용표현이다
'came around'의 의미(마음이 풀리다)를 모르고 'came back'처럼 쓰는 경우 — come around는 태도나 입장이 바뀌는 것
'feel lighter'를 'feel more light'처럼 비교급 형태로 쓰는 오류 — lighter가 이미 비교급

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 인생에서 후회되는 선택을 솔직하게 이야기한다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You know what I keep thinking about? Turning down that job offer five years ago.
dialogue.ko: 내가 계속 생각하는 게 뭔지 알아? 5년 전에 그 직장 제안을 거절한 거.
alt_en: You know what I can't stop thinking about? Saying no to that job offer five years ago.
I keep coming back to the same thing — turning down that job offer five years back.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I remember that. The overseas position, right? Why do you think you said no?
dialogue.ko: 그거 기억해. 해외 포지션이었지? 왜 거절했던 것 같아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Fear, I think. I was, uh, scared of failing in a new place. And I convinced myself I had good reasons.
dialogue.ko: 두려움이었던 것 같아. 새로운 곳에서 실패하는 게, 어, 무서웠어. 그리고 좋은 이유가 있다고 스스로 설득했어.
alt_en: Fear, mainly. I was scared of failing somewhere new. And I convinced myself I had valid reasons.
Honestly, fear. I was afraid of failing in an unfamiliar place — and I told myself I had good reasons to say no.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's pretty self-aware. Most people just say the timing wasn't right.
dialogue.ko: 꽤 자기 인식이 높은 거야. 대부분은 그냥 타이밍이 안 좋았다고 해.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's what I said too, actually. 'The timing wasn't right.' But — I mean — that was just an excuse.
dialogue.ko: 나도 그렇게 말했어, 사실. '타이밍이 안 맞았다.' 근데 — 있잖아 — 그건 그냥 핑계였어.
alt_en: Actually, that's exactly what I said at the time. 'The timing wasn't right.' But honestly, that was just an excuse.
That was my line too — 'bad timing.' But looking back, I know it was just an excuse.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: It's striking that you can see that now. Recognizing a rationalization takes real honesty.
dialogue.ko: 지금 그걸 볼 수 있다는 게 인상적이야. 합리화를 알아채는 건 진짜 솔직함이 필요한 거야.
dialogue.recast_note: 'convinced myself I had good reasons'를 'rationalization'으로 명시 recast — 자기 설득을 심리 개념어로 환언

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Do you think regret is useful, or does it just — I don't know — drag you down?
dialogue.ko: 후회가 유용하다고 생각해, 아니면 그냥 — 모르겠어 — 끌어내리기만 하는 건지?
alt_en: Do you think regret serves a purpose, or does it just drag you down?
Is regret actually useful, or does it just hold you back?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Useful in small doses. When it teaches you something. When it keeps cycling — that's when it becomes a trap.
dialogue.ko: 적당히는 유용하지. 뭔가를 가르쳐줄 때. 계속 반복될 때 — 그게 함정이 되는 거야.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: That's a good way to frame it. I think I learned that I let fear make decisions for me.
dialogue.ko: 그렇게 생각하니 좋네. 두려움이 나 대신 결정을 내리게 했다는 걸 배웠어.
alt_en: That's a helpful way to put it. I've learned that I was letting fear make my decisions.
Good way to think about it. What I take from it is that I let fear call the shots for me.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: And knowing that — that's the part that can actually change things going forward.
dialogue.ko: 그걸 아는 거 — 그게 앞으로를 실제로 바꿀 수 있는 부분이야.

key_expressions.note: 실제로는 합리화인데 마치 이유가 있는 것처럼 자신을 설득하는 행위
감정적 결정을 논리적으로 포장하는 심리 메커니즘

key_expressions.en: let fear make decisions for me
key_expressions.note: 결정의 주도권을 감정에 양도하는 행위를 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'turning down'을 'refusing'으로만 대체하는 경우 — turn down이 구어에서 훨씬 자연스럽고 빈번하게 쓰인다
'drag you down'을 'pull you down'으로 대체하는 경우 — drag는 '질질 끌다'는 느낌으로, pull보다 더 무거운 뉘앙스
'in small doses'의 비유를 이해 못하는 경우 — 약을 소량 복용하듯 '적당히'를 뜻하는 구어 표현

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 만약 복권에 당첨된다면 어떻게 할지 이야기한다

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Okay, hypothetically — if you won the lottery tomorrow, what's the first thing you'd do?
dialogue.ko: 가정이야 — 내일 복권에 당첨된다면, 제일 먼저 뭐 할 것 같아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Honestly? I'd pay off my parents' house first. Like, that's — that's not even a question.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히? 부모님 집 대출부터 갚겠어. 그건 — 그건 고민도 안 해.
alt_en: Honestly, I'd clear my parents' mortgage first. No question about it.
First thing? Pay off my parents' house. That's not even a debate.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's really sweet. After that — would you keep working?
dialogue.ko: 진짜 좋다. 그 다음은 — 일은 계속 할 것 같아?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Probably, yeah. I'd go crazy just sitting around. But I'd want to, um, work on my own terms.
dialogue.ko: 아마 그렇겠지. 그냥 앉아 있으면 미쳐버릴 것 같아. 근데 음, 내 조건대로 일하고 싶어.
alt_en: Yeah, probably. I'd lose my mind doing nothing. But I'd want to work on my own schedule.
I think so. Just sitting around would drive me crazy. I'd want to work — but on my own terms.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: So you'd set up your own thing — be your own boss. That sounds like the real freedom.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 네 일을 차리겠다는 거네 — 자기가 보스가 되는 거. 그게 진짜 자유인 것 같아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'work on my own terms'를 'set up your own thing / be your own boss'로 recast — 조건 추구를 자영업·독립으로 구체화

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Exactly. Maybe open a small café or something. Nothing huge — just, like, something I actually love.
dialogue.ko: 딱 맞아. 작은 카페 같은 거 열 수도 있지. 크지 않아도 되고 — 그냥, 내가 진짜 좋아하는 것.
alt_en: Exactly. Maybe open a small café or a little shop — nothing huge, just something I genuinely love.
Right. Like a small café maybe. Not anything big — just something I'm actually passionate about.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: I love that. Okay, and travel — anywhere on your list?
dialogue.ko: 너무 좋다. 자 그럼, 여행은 — 가고 싶은 데 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: South America, for sure. I'd do a really slow trip — two or three months, no rush.
dialogue.ko: 남미, 당연히. 진짜 느린 여행 할 거야 — 두세 달, 서두르지 않고.
alt_en: South America, without a doubt. A slow trip — two, maybe three months with no agenda.
Definitely South America. I'd take it slow — two or three months, nowhere to be.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That sounds dreamy. Now I want to win the lottery just to come with you.
dialogue.ko: 너무 좋겠다. 나도 복권 당첨돼서 같이 가고 싶어졌어.

key_expressions.note: mortgage, loan 등을 완납할 때 쓰는 표현
외부 압력 없이 스스로 정한 방식을 따른다는 의미
시간적 여유가 있음을 나타내는 가벼운 표현

common_mistakes_ko: 'pay off the loan'을 'pay the loan'처럼 off 없이 쓰는 오류 — off가 완납의 뉘앙스를 담당한다
'on my own terms'를 'with my own conditions'처럼 직역하는 실수 — terms가 여기서 조건/방식을 뜻한다
'I'd go crazy' 대신 'I will go crazy'처럼 가정 상황에서 will을 쓰는 시제 오류 — would가 가정법에 맞다

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 각자 10년 후 어떤 삶을 살고 있을지 상상해본다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey — where do you picture yourself ten years from now?
dialogue.ko: 있잖아 — 10년 후에 어디에 있을 것 같아?
alt_en: Hey, where do you see yourself in ten years?
Okay, ten years from now — what does your life look like?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Honestly? Living somewhere quieter. Maybe with a dog. How about you?
dialogue.ko: 솔직히? 더 조용한 데 살고 있을 것 같아. 아마 강아지랑. 너는?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I — um — hope I'm running my own business. Something small but steady.
dialogue.ko: 나는 — 음 — 내 사업을 운영하고 있었으면 해. 작지만 안정적인 뭔가.
alt_en: I hope I'm running my own business by then — something small and sustainable.
Ideally, I'd be running my own little business. Small but steady.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That's very specific. Do you already have a direction in mind?
dialogue.ko: 꽤 구체적이다. 이미 방향이 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sort of. I keep coming back to something in education — like online courses or workshops.
dialogue.ko: 어느 정도. 자꾸 교육 쪽으로 생각이 가 — 온라인 강좌나 워크샵 같은 거.
alt_en: Kind of. I keep gravitating toward something in education — like teaching online or running workshops.
Sort of. I always come back to education — online courses, workshops, that kind of thing.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: That tracks with who you are. You've always been the person who explains things clearly.
dialogue.ko: 너답다. 항상 뭔가를 명확하게 설명해주는 사람이었잖아.
dialogue.recast_note: 'online courses or workshops'라는 구체 아이디어를 'who you are / explains things clearly'로 recast — 희망을 개인 정체성과 연결

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ha, thanks. I also — well — hope to travel more. I've been putting it off too long.
dialogue.ko: 하, 고마워. 나도 — 뭐 — 여행을 더 많이 하고 싶어. 너무 오래 미뤘어.
alt_en: Ha, thanks. I also hope to travel more. I've been putting it off for too long.
Thanks. And I'd like to travel more — I've been putting that off forever.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Ten years is plenty of time if you actually start planning. Don't let it stay hypothetical.
dialogue.ko: 제대로 계획하기 시작하면 10년은 충분해. 가정에만 머물지 마.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: You're right. I should stop dreaming and start doing.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 꿈꾸기를 그만하고 실행에 옮겨야 해.
alt_en: Fair point. I need to stop just dreaming and start actually doing.
You're right. Time to stop dreaming and start making it happen.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: There you go.
dialogue.ko: 바로 그거야.

key_expressions.en: That tracks with who you are
key_expressions.note: 누군가의 선택·행동이 그 사람의 성격과 일치할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 표현
해야 할 일을 계속 나중으로 미루는 행위
계획에만 머무르지 말고 행동에 나서라는 의미

common_mistakes_ko: 'putting it off'을 'delaying it'으로만 대체하는 경우 — put off는 구어에서 훨씬 자주 쓰이는 선택이다
'Ten years is plenty of time'에서 'enough time' 사용도 가능하지만 'plenty of'가 더 강조적
'That tracks' 단독 사용은 최근 미국 구어에서 자주 쓰임 — 'That makes sense'와 유사하나 더 비공식적

scenarios.context_ko: 친구와 시간 여행이 가능하다면 어디로 갈지 상상하며 대화한다

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Hey — totally random, but if you could time travel, would you go to the past or the future?
dialogue.ko: 야 — 완전 뜬금없는데, 시간 여행을 할 수 있다면 과거로 가겠어 아니면 미래?
alt_en: Okay, random question — time travel: past or future?
If you could time travel, would you head to the past or go to the future?

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: Future, no question. I want to see how things turn out. You?
dialogue.ko: 미래, 당연히. 어떻게 되는지 보고 싶어. 너는?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Past, for me. I'd — um — want to see the 1960s. Like, the music, the streets, everything.
dialogue.ko: 나는 과거. 1960년대를 — 음 — 보고 싶어. 음악이랑, 거리, 모든 게.
alt_en: Past, for me. I'd want to see the 1960s — the music, the energy, the whole vibe.
The past. I'd go straight to the 1960s — the music, the streets, the whole scene.

dialogue.speaker: AI
dialogue.en: The '60s — that era had a real intensity to it. Did you have a specific place in mind?
dialogue.ko: 60년대 — 그 시대는 진짜 강렬함이 있었지. 구체적인 장소가 있어?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yeah, New York. I keep imagining, like, just walking down Greenwich Village and hearing live jazz coming out of a door.
dialogue.ko: 응, 뉴욕. 자꾸 상상하는 게, 그냥 그리니치 빌리지를 걷다가 어느 문에서 라이브 재즈가 흘러나오는 거.
alt_en: New York City. I imagine just walking through Greenwich Village and hearing live jazz spilling out of some doorway.
